settings.accounts.list.desc.text: Add an account (signed in, or a server) and the connections agents choose on it, and turn accounts on in this workspace. Drag accounts into your order: a new agent gets the first connection of the first account that's on here.
settings.accounts.list.desc.note: What the list "Accounts & Connections" does, under its title (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107: one order of accounts for every coding agent CLI; a new agent gets the first connection of the first account on in the workspace).

settings.accounts.list.tip.text: A sign-in account is a folder of its own that Hive made, signed in with the CLI's own sign-in in your browser: Hive never sees or keeps its login. Its conversations and memory are shared with your other accounts through a link to the CLI's projects folder. Removing an account deletes its folder and its login on this PC, never your conversations. GitHub Copilot signs in once for the whole PC, in Provider Setup: its account is that sign-in.
settings.accounts.list.tip.note: The info tip of the list "Accounts & Connections" (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): more on what it does and when it applies. Provider Setup names a dialog.

settings.accounts.list.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Accounts & Connections, HI-2107): the list of accounts, each with its connections.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.d.text: The environment variables Hive leaves out when it runs Claude Code on a connection (its sign-in, its checks, Set Up and its agents), by name: a key, token, request header, server, provider switch or model set on this PC can't stand in for the connection's own. A server connection's own (its server, key and models) are set after. Wrong, a variable Claude Code reads as a login, a header or a server could make a connection run as someone else, or send a key elsewhere.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.d.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: sign-in variables left out" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.e.text: The field of `claude auth status --json` with the email a connection's folder is signed in as. Wrong, Hive can't tell who a connection is signed in as, and can't warn when its login changes.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.e.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: email field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.text: The field of `claude auth status --json` that says whether a connection's folder is signed in. Wrong, Hive can't tell, and its sign-in connections show "Couldn't check".
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: signed-in field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.text: The names of the files in a connection's folder that change when Claude Code signs in or out there, as a regular expression. Hive watches them (it never reads them) and checks the connection again when one changes. Wrong, a /login or /logout typed in an agent's pane is only found at the connection's next check.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.l.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: login files" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep /login and /logout as they are (commands).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.text: The field of a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code's first-run screens were answered there (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: set-up field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `.claude.json` as it is (a file name); "Needs set up" is a state Hive shows: use its name as Hive shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.text: The field of `claude auth status --json` with the organisation's id a connection's folder is signed in to. With the email, it tells two logins apart. Wrong, Hive can't tell who a connection is signed in as.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.o.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: organisation field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.p.text: The field of `claude auth status --json` with a connection's plan ("max"), shown beside its email in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Wrong, no plan is shown.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.p.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: plan field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status --json` and "max" as they are.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.s.text: How long Hive gives `claude auth status` to say who a connection's folder is signed in as. Past it, the connection shows "Couldn't check", never signed out.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.s.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: sign-in check timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `claude auth status` as it is (a command).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.t.text: The field of a folder's entry under `projects` in a connection folder's `.claude.json` that says Claude Code was told to trust that folder (read only). Wrong, every Claude Code connection on in a workspace shows "Needs set up" in Settings → Accounts & Connections.
settings.advanced.claude-code.accounts.t.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: trusted folder field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Keep `projects` and `.claude.json` as they are; "Needs set up" is a state Hive shows: use its name as Hive shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.autoModeSe.text: Claude Code offers, now and then in auto mode, to read the project, your recent sessions and optionally your shell history and other repositories, to teach auto mode about your environment. Hive never answers it: the agent waits for you. Off, Hive's Claude Code agents are started with the offer turned off for that launch (nothing is written to Claude Code's files, and auto mode decides as before); /auto-mode-setup still runs it when you want.
settings.advanced.claude-code.autoModeSe.note: What the advanced setting "Offer auto mode's environment setup" is for, and what happens when it is off (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959). /auto-mode-setup is Claude Code's command: keep it as it is.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Auto mode is one of Claude Code's permission modes.

settings.advanced.claude-code.connection.text: The model names Ollama runs on ollama.com rather than on this PC (its cloud models, such as gpt-oss:120b-cloud), as a regular expression, for an Ollama connection's models typed in rather than read from Ollama (Read Models asks Ollama, which says). Such a connection's sessions aren't free (local). Wrong, a cloud model typed in is counted as free, or a local one as not free.
settings.advanced.claude-code.connection.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: Ollama cloud models" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Ollama, ollama.com and Read Models (a button) are names; "free (local)" is how Hive shows the cost of sessions run only on this PC.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Ollama is a product's name; its cloud models run on ollama.com.

settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.comma.text: What Hive types into Claude Code, then Enter, to end it once its lane has ended and its turn is over, so it exits by itself rather than being killed. Wrong, Claude Code isn't ended by it and is killed after the exit grace.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.comma.note: What the advanced setting "Lane's end: exit command" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). A lane is a card loop.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.grace.text: How long Hive gives Claude Code to exit by itself after typing its exit command at a lane's end, before killing it. It took {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} when recorded.
settings.advanced.claude-code.exit.grace.note: What the advanced setting "Lane's end: exit grace" is for (Settings → Advanced). {took} is how long Claude Code took to exit when recorded, in seconds (1.9).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.text: The hook events Hive knows Claude Code sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known events" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.text: The top-level fields Hive knows Claude Code sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a Claude Code update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.know.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known fields" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT.text: How long Claude Code waits for Hive's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Hive doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.preT.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: before a tool, timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time.text: How long Claude Code waits for Hive to take one of its hooks (a turn starting or ending, a notification). Hive answers at once; raise it only if Hive's log shows hooks timing out on a slow machine.
settings.advanced.claude-code.hooks.time.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.text: A connection's projects folder is a link to Claude Code's own, so Claude Code asked you before each memory it saved there. Each Claude Code agent on a connection is given its project's auto memory folder by its real path: the same folder, so it saves memories without asking, as it does without a connection. Nothing more is allowed, and nothing is written to Claude Code's files. Off, Claude Code asks before each memory on a connection.
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.note: What the advanced setting "Auto memory by its real path on connections" is for, and what happens when it is off (Settings → Advanced, HI-1899). Auto memory is Claude Code's own notes it keeps per project; a connection is an account Hive signs a CLI in with; "projects" is a folder's name: keep it.

settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.text: Auto memory by its real path on connections
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.rea.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Auto memory is Claude Code's own notes it keeps per project; a connection is an account Hive signs a CLI in with.

settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.set.text: The Claude Code setting that names its auto memory folder, which Hive sets on a connection (Auto memory by its real path on connections) and leaves alone where you set it yourself. Wrong, Claude Code ignores it and asks before each memory on a connection.
settings.advanced.claude-code.memory.set.note: What the advanced setting "Auto memory folder setting" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1899). "Auto memory by its real path on connections" is another advanced setting's title: keep it as translated there.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Auto memory is Claude Code's own notes it keeps per project.

settings.advanced.claude-code.mouse.righ.text: Right-click in a Claude Code pane is Hive's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection, or pastes. Turned on, Hive passes right-clicks to Claude Code instead. Claude Code doesn't use the mouse at its prompt, so there a right-click then does nothing: copy and paste with Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V.
settings.advanced.claude-code.mouse.righ.note: What the advanced setting "Pass right-click to Claude Code" is for (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code). Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys: use the key names your language uses.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.outage.con.text: What a StopFailure hook's message says when Claude Code couldn't reach its API after its retries: with Resume agents after a connection drops on, Hive waits for the connection and resumes the agent. Wrong, such agents stay stopped.
settings.advanced.claude-code.outage.con.note: What the advanced setting "Connection dropped: StopFailure message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Resume agents after a connection drops is the title of another advanced setting.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.m.text: Hive starts Claude Code with --strict-mcp-config, so its sessions get only the MCP servers the workspace gives them. Turned off, the servers in your own Claude Code config and the project's .mcp.json load beside them, as they would outside Hive (Claude Code may ask you to approve a project's new servers first). The workspace's servers, Hive's own hive among them, win over yours of the same name.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.m.note: What the advanced setting "Only the workspace's MCP servers" does (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code). --strict-mcp-config is a command-line option and .mcp.json a file name: keep them. hive is the name of Hive's MCP server.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default. MCP is a protocol's name.

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.text: When the Hive Assistant runs on Claude Code, Hive passes --allowedTools with the Hive tools its Control settings let it use without asking, so Claude Code doesn't ask before them. Turned off, Claude Code asks before each Hive tool as its own permission mode says. Control still decides what the Assistant may do either way. Agents' Hive tools are never pre-approved on Claude Code.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.note: What the advanced setting "Pre-approve the Assistant's Hive tools" does (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code). --allowedTools is a command-line option: keep it. Control is the name of the Assistant's settings page.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default.

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.text: When the Hive Assistant's conversation resumes, Hive starts Claude Code with --system-prompt-snapshot off, so the Assistant follows its role and Control settings as they are now. Turned off, Hive leaves the flag out and Claude Code keeps sending the instructions it recorded when the conversation began, until it compacts: a change to the Assistant's settings may not reach it until then. --system-prompt-snapshot in Extra arguments wins either way.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.note: What the advanced setting "Resume the Assistant with its current instructions" does (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code). --system-prompt-snapshot off is a command-line option and its value: keep them. Control is the name of the Assistant's settings page.

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.text: Resume the Assistant with its current instructions
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.p.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default.

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.s.text: Hive starts Claude Code with a status line of its own, which sends Hive the session's model, context, cost and plan limits for the agent's footer and shows nothing under the input. Turned off, the status line in your Claude Code settings shows again: Hive's command still reads the status, then runs yours with the same input Claude Code gives it and shows what it prints. With no status line of yours, nothing changes.
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.s.note: What the advanced setting "Hive's status line in place of yours" does (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code).

settings.advanced.claude-code.override.s.text: Hive's status line in place of yours
settings.advanced.claude-code.override.s.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under Claude Code): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default. The status line is the line Claude Code shows under its input.

settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cle.text: Claude Code's Ctrl+U deletes one row of a draft that wraps onto several, so before Hive types into it, it presses Ctrl+U a key at a time until the input box (Screen: input box) shows empty. This is how long Hive waits for Claude Code to show each key's effect. Not shown in time, Hive types nothing and tries again later: too short, and a busy Claude Code makes Hive put its messages off more often.
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cle.note: What the advanced setting "Clearing the input: wait for each key" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1979). Ctrl+U names keys: use the key names your language uses. "Screen: input box" is another advanced setting's title: use its translation.

settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cle.text: Clearing the input: wait for each key
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cle.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cli.text: What a prompt hook's text starts with when Claude Code starts a turn by itself, such as when a background task ends. Hive never reports such a turn to the Hive Assistant as your reply. Wrong, a background task's end soon after you pressed Enter in the agent's pane can be reported as your reply.
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cli.note: What the advanced setting "Prompt hook: Claude Code's own turn" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cli.text: Prompt hook: Claude Code's own turn
settings.advanced.claude-code.prompt.cli.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.atte.text: The field of that entry with which try it is (1, 2…). Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.atte.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: retry entry's try field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.chec.text: How long a working Claude Code session has to go without a hook before Hive looks at the end of its transcript for a wait to retry its model request, then every 15 seconds while it stays quiet.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.chec.note: What the advanced setting "Retry wait: look after" does (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("20 s"). A retry wait: the coding agent waiting to try its model request again.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.maxF.text: The field of that entry with how many tries it makes in all. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.maxF.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: retry entry's tries field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.stat.text: The field of that entry's error with the HTTP status that refused the request (429: rate-limited). With none, the service couldn't be reached. Wrong, every wait shows as the service unreachable.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.stat.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: retry error's status field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.subt.text: The kind of transcript entry Claude Code writes each time its model request fails and it tries again (rate-limited, or the service unreachable). Hive reads the latest and shows the wait as the agent's status. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.subt.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: retry entry" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. A retry: the coding agent trying its model request again after it failed.

settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.wait.text: The field of that entry with how long Claude Code waits before the next try, in milliseconds. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.claude-code.retry.wait.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: retry entry's wait field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.safeguard..text: Claude Code's note in its transcript when its safety classifier stops a response, and the notice it adds for the model (#606). Wrong, Hive misses such stops: no shield on the agent's pane, and Performance doesn't count them.
settings.advanced.claude-code.safeguard..note: What the advanced setting "Safeguard stop: transcript note" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.safeguard..text: Claude Code's question after a safeguard stop, whether to switch models, told by its open dialog's choices in the lines it wrote last. Hive shows the agent waiting for you, and why, while it is open; wrong, the agent shows only "Claude needs your permission".
settings.advanced.claude-code.safeguard..note: What the advanced setting "Safeguard stop: question" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.idl.text: A question Claude Code puts on its screen by itself after a turn, sending Hive nothing ("Teach auto mode about your environment?"), as a line of its own in a dialog that replaces its input box or is drawn under it (the same words above the input box, in a prompt or a reply, aren't it). While it shows, Hive shows the agent waiting for you with the question, and types nothing into it: Enter would answer it. Wrong, Hive types its wakes into the question.
settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.idl.note: What the advanced setting "Screen: question while idle" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959). The quoted question is Claude Code's own, in English: keep it as it is.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.inp.text: Claude Code's input box, between two rules, its first group what it holds after its prompt mark. Hive reads it to tell that a line it typed is gone from the input (a screen of the CLI's took it), and then types it again. Wrong, such a line stays held, and nothing more is typed into the agent until you press Enter there.
settings.advanced.claude-code.screen.inp.note: What the advanced setting "Screen: input box" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959). A rule: a horizontal line drawn across the terminal.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.signIn.sto.text: The error a StopFailure hook names when Claude Code's sign-in was refused (expired, revoked, an invalid key): Hive shows the agent signed out and offers to carry on once it's renewed (#309). Any other error ends the turn as failed.
settings.advanced.claude-code.signIn.sto.note: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: StopFailure error" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.text: The plan limits' field for the 5-hour window.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.note: What the advanced setting "Status line: 5-hour limit field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.text: The top-level fields Hive knows Claude Code sends in its status line. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a status line with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.note: What the advanced setting "Status line: known fields" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.text: The status line's field with a subscription's limits (the 5-hour and weekly use the status bar shows). Wrong, Hive shows no plan limits for Claude Code.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.note: What the advanced setting "Status line: plan limits field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.text: A limit's field with the percentage used.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.note: What the advanced setting "Status line: percentage used field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.text: The plan limits' field for the weekly window.
settings.advanced.claude-code.statusLine.note: What the advanced setting "Status line: weekly limit field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.d.text: The field of that result with what the subagent was asked to do, in a few words. Wrong, Hive still counts it but has no description of it.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.d.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: background subagent's description field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.i.text: The field of that result with the subagent's id, which its notification names when it ends. Wrong, Hive doesn't count background subagents.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.i.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: background subagent's id field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.l.text: The status of the Agent tool's result when it runs a subagent (or a workflow) in the background (#1584). Wrong, Hive doesn't count those subagents, and shows the agent finished while they work.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.l.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: background subagent launched" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.r.text: The field of a message's result with the id of a finished subagent the message started again. Wrong, Hive doesn't count a resumed subagent while it works.
settings.advanced.claude-code.subagent.r.note: What the advanced setting "Transcript: resumed subagent field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.trust.prom.text: Claude Code's question before a folder's first session. Hive shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.claude-code.trust.prom.note: What the advanced setting "Trust question" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.claude-code.turnScreen.text: Claude Code's line above its input when the last turn is done ("✻ Worked for 12s · done 16:52"). When Hive missed a turn's end, it takes this on screen to mean the agent is idle; wrong, it leaves such an agent's status unknown, with Mark idle.

settings.advanced.codex.accounts.uneleva.text: Turned on, Hive runs Codex on a connection (its agents, its Set Up and its checks) in Codex's non-admin Windows sandbox, passing -c windows.sandbox="unelevated" each time, unless the connection's own config.toml chooses a sandbox. Nothing is written to Codex's config, and Codex on its own folder (~/.codex) runs as you've set it up. What it gains: no Administrator (UAC) prompts, and setting up one Codex folder no longer resets the sandbox's shared password, which makes the others ask for Administrator permission again. What it loses: commands run as you rather than as separate sandbox accounts, and their network is blocked by environment settings only, not by the firewall. Unchanged: writes outside the project's folders are still refused, and the first time a connection works in a project it still grants its permissions over the project's files once. Either way, Codex's commands can still read other connections' login files. Windows only.
settings.advanced.codex.accounts.uneleva.note: What the advanced setting "Connections: use Codex's non-admin sandbox" does (Settings → Advanced, under Codex). -c windows.sandbox="unelevated" is a command-line option, and config.toml and ~/.codex are a file and a folder: keep them as they are. UAC is Windows' User Account Control.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Codex's non-admin sandbox is its Windows sandbox that needs no Administrator permission.

settings.advanced.codexPermissions.desc.note: What the advanced setting is for (Settings → Advanced, under Codex). {label} is Codex's own name for a preset and {mode} Hive's id for the mode (read-only, ask…), both in English: keep them as they are.

settings.advanced.codexPermissions.title.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under Codex). /permissions is a Codex command and {label} Codex's own name for a preset, in English: keep both as they are.

settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.con.text: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the conversation's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.con.note: What the advanced setting "Compaction: conversation tokens field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sum.text: The field of a compaction's end, in Copilot's session file, with the summary it carries on from: the Sessions tab shows it with the compaction.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sum.note: What the advanced setting "Compaction: summary field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sys.text: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the system prompt's tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.sys.note: What the advanced setting "Compaction: system prompt tokens field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.too.text: The field of a compaction's start and end, in Copilot's session file, with the tool definitions' tokens: one of the three parts of the context before and after it, in usage and the Sessions tab.
settings.advanced.copilot.compaction.too.note: What the advanced setting "Compaction: tool definition tokens field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.exit.armed.des.text: What Copilot shows after one Ctrl+C at its prompt, meaning the next one exits. When Hive stops Copilot, it presses Ctrl+C again once this shows. If it no longer matches, Hive keeps pressing Ctrl+C until Copilot exits, which takes longer.
settings.advanced.copilot.exit.armed.des.note: What the advanced setting "Stop: exit hint" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.copilot.exit.armed.tit.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.exit.graceSeco.text: When Hive stops Copilot (Stop, Restart, closing a project or quitting), how long it gives Copilot to exit by itself after its Ctrl+C before killing it. Copilot writes the session's token totals only as it exits by itself: one killed first loses them. It took up to {took, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} on a busy machine (#716); quitting Hive or closing a workspace waits up to this long, and a second more, for a Copilot that hangs.
settings.advanced.copilot.exit.graceSeco.note: What the advanced setting "Stop: exit grace" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). {took} is the longest Copilot was seen to take, in seconds (2.4).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownEve.text: The hook events Hive knows GitHub Copilot sends. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook named outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownEve.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known events" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownFie.text: The top-level fields Hive knows GitHub Copilot sends in its hooks. With Settings → Advanced → Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI on, a hook with a field outside this list saves a capture of the agent's recent events: often the first sign that a GitHub Copilot update changed something. Add a field here once you know it is harmless.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.knownFie.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: known fields" is for (Settings → Advanced). Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI is another setting's title: use it as Settings shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.preToolU.text: How long Copilot waits for Hive's answer before a tool runs (an edit waits for a file lock). If Hive doesn't answer in time, the tool goes ahead.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.preToolU.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: before a tool, timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.timeoutS.text: How long Copilot waits for Hive to take one of its hooks.
settings.advanced.copilot.hooks.timeoutS.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks: timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.mouse.rightCli.text: Right-click in a Copilot pane is Hive's, as in every pane: it copies the terminal's selection (Shift+drag), or pastes. Turned on, Hive passes right-clicks to Copilot instead, which copies its own selection (a drag) with them, as its footer says.
settings.advanced.copilot.mouse.rightCli.note: What the advanced setting "Pass right-click to Copilot" is for (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). Shift+drag names a key and a mouse action: use the key names your language uses.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.outage.connect.text: What Copilot's error says when it couldn't reach its model's API after its retries: with Resume agents after a connection drops on, Hive waits for the connection and resumes the agent. Wrong, such agents stay stopped.
settings.advanced.copilot.outage.connect.note: What the advanced setting "Connection dropped: error message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). Resume agents after a connection drops is the title of another advanced setting.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.allMc.text: Hive starts Copilot with --allow-all-mcp-server-instructions, so Copilot puts the hive server's instructions (Hive's guidance for agents) in its system prompt, and the instructions of the other servers its agents get too. Turned off, Copilot includes only the servers it allows by itself, and Hive gives its guidance as custom instructions instead.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.allMc.note: What the advanced setting "Include every MCP server's instructions" does (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). --allow-all-mcp-server-instructions is a command-line option: keep it. hive is the name of Hive's MCP server.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default. MCP is a protocol's name.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.mcpIs.text: Hive starts Copilot with --disable-builtin-mcps, and --disable-mcp-server for each server in your own Copilot config and the project's, so its sessions get only the MCP servers the workspace gives them. Turned off, those and Copilot's built-in GitHub servers load beside them, as they would outside Hive. The workspace's servers, Hive's own hive among them, win over yours of the same name.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.mcpIs.note: What the advanced setting "Only the workspace's MCP servers" does (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). --disable-builtin-mcps and --disable-mcp-server are command-line options: keep them. hive is the name of Hive's MCP server.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default. MCP is a protocol's name.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.noAut.text: Hive starts Copilot with --no-auto-update and COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false (its sessions, and checking its sign-in and models), so it runs the version installed and a download never changes it between a session's restarts; Update in Provider Setup updates it when you choose. Turned off, Hive sets neither and Copilot updates itself as it would outside Hive (your own COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE still applies).
settings.advanced.copilot.override.noAut.note: What the advanced setting "Don't let Copilot update itself" does (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). --no-auto-update is a command-line option and COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false an environment variable: keep them. Update is a button's name and Provider Setup a dialog's.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.preAp.text: Hive starts Copilot with --allow-tool for Hive's tools (for the Hive Assistant, only those its Control settings let it use without asking), so Copilot doesn't ask before them in any mode. Turned off, Copilot asks before them as its own permission mode says. What an agent or the Assistant may do with them is still decided by Hive.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.preAp.note: What the advanced setting "Pre-approve Hive's tools" does (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). --allow-tool is a command-line option: keep it. Control is the name of the Assistant's settings page.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.strip.text: Hive leaves GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, which other tools set, out of Copilot's environment, so a token left there never signs Copilot agents in to another account; COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, set for Copilot, is kept. Turned off, Copilot gets them and signs in with them before its own login, as it would outside Hive, and Provider Setup shows that sign-in.
settings.advanced.copilot.override.strip.note: What the advanced setting "Keep GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN from Copilot" does (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN and COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN are environment variables: keep them. Provider Setup is a dialog's name.

settings.advanced.copilot.override.strip.text: Keep GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN from Copilot
settings.advanced.copilot.override.strip.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): one of Hive's overrides of the CLI, on by default. GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are environment variables: keep them.

settings.advanced.copilot.question.field.text: The field of the question tool's input, in Copilot's hooks, with the question's text. When it is wrong, the agent shows only Copilot's own notice while it waits for your answer.
settings.advanced.copilot.question.field.note: What the advanced setting "Question: text field" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.question.tool..text: The name Copilot's hooks give its tool that asks you a question. Hive shows that tool's question while the agent waits for your answer; when it doesn't match, the agent shows only Copilot's own notice.
settings.advanced.copilot.question.tool..note: What the advanced setting "Question: tool name" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d.text: Copilot only says it has started with the first prompt, so Hive takes its footer on screen to mean it is ready.
settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.d.note: What the advanced setting "Ready footer" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.copilot.ready.footer.t.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.retry.context..text: Where Copilot's error hook says a recoverable error happened when it is a model call it tries again (rate-limited, or the service unreachable). Hive shows the agent's status as waiting to retry until Copilot goes on. Wrong, a waiting agent just shows Working.
settings.advanced.copilot.retry.context..note: What the advanced setting "Retry: error context" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. A retry: the coding agent trying its model request again after it failed.

settings.advanced.copilot.retry.message..text: How that hook words why the call failed: a regular expression whose named group status is the HTTP status that refused it, whose group limited matches the words of a rate limit (429), or whose group network matches when the service couldn't be reached. Copilot's hook gives the service's own error, often with no status. Wrong, the wait shows without its reason.
settings.advanced.copilot.retry.message..note: What the advanced setting "Retry: error message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). status, limited and network are the names of the regular expression's groups: keep them.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe.text: A session error's message, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused, when its type doesn't say so.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorMe.note: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: error message" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy.text: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its sign-in was refused or is missing (#309): Hive shows the agent signed out.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.errorTy.note: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: error type" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes.text: The message of Copilot's ErrorOccurred hook that means a model call was refused for the sign-in: the turn ends signed out. Another error that ends the turn ends it as failed.
settings.advanced.copilot.signIn.hookMes.note: What the advanced setting "Sign-in refused: ErrorOccurred hook" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d.text: Copilot's question before a folder's first session. Hive shows the agent as waiting for you while it is on screen.
settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.d.note: What the advanced setting "Trust question" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.copilot.trust.prompt.t.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilot.turnFailed.err.text: A session error's type, in Copilot's session file, that means its turn ended because a model call failed after Copilot's retries (it sends no Stop then): Hive ends the turn as failed, with Copilot's message. Wrong, such an agent shows working until you look.
settings.advanced.copilot.turnFailed.err.note: What the advanced setting "Turn failed: error type" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc.text: Copilot's footer in the {mode} mode ("{footer}"){shared, select, yes {, which Ask and Accept edits share (Hive tells them apart by the mode the session started in)} other {}}. Hive reads an agent's mode from its footer (the mode found last on screen), and switches modes by pressing Shift+Tab until the footer shows the one wanted; wrong, Hive doesn't see the agent in that mode, and can't switch to it without a restart.
settings.advanced.copilotFooter.desc.note: What the advanced setting is for (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot). {mode} is a mode's name; {footer} is Copilot's own footer text, in English: keep it as it is. {shared} is yes for the footer two modes share.

settings.advanced.copilotFooter.title.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced, under GitHub Copilot): the footer Copilot shows in a mode. {mode} is the mode's name.

settings.advanced.data.desc.note: What the setting "Settings file" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.data.tip.text: Project settings live in each project's .hive folder; workspace settings in the workspace .hive folder.
settings.advanced.data.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Settings file" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.error.badPattern.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {why} the browser engine's own reason, in English.

settings.advanced.error.boolean.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; true and false are the values as written: keep them.

settings.advanced.error.choice.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {choices} lists the values it takes as advanced.json writes them (allow, ask, block): keep them.

settings.advanced.error.field.text: {title} takes a field name: letters, digits and _ (not starting with a digit).
settings.advanced.error.field.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken: it must be a field name of a CLI's data. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.list.text: {title} takes 1 to 10 names (letters, digits, - and _), as a list or separated by commas.
settings.advanced.error.list.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.text: {title} would match anything (it matches empty text).
settings.advanced.error.matchesAll.note: Why an advanced setting's new value (a regular expression) isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.number.text: {title} takes a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.error.number.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {min} and {max} are numbers.

settings.advanced.error.oneLine.text: {title} takes one line of at most {most} characters.
settings.advanced.error.oneLine.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title; {most} a number of characters.

settings.advanced.error.pattern.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken (Settings → Advanced). {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.error.text.note: Why an advanced setting's new value isn't taken. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.text: Move an account's agents to another account when it reaches the share of its limit set on it in Settings → Accounts & Connections. Turned off, no account moves its agents and moves waiting for an agent's turn to end are dropped; the rules are kept.
settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.note: What the advanced setting "Move agents at a usage threshold" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Settings → Accounts & Connections names a section.

settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.text: Move agents at a usage threshold
settings.advanced.hive.accounts.usageMov.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. An account in Settings → Accounts & Connections can move its agents to another account when it has used a share of its plan's limit.

settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.text: While the Hive Assistant's journal is on, Hive gives it a short view of the workspace when it starts and after each compaction: what is under way and waiting, and the journal's recent entries. Turned off, it gets none from its next start or compaction on, a running Assistant too, and reads what it needs with its tools.
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.note: What the advanced setting "The Assistant starts with Hive's start view" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.text: The Assistant starts with Hive's start view
settings.advanced.hive.assistant.startVi.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The start view is what Hive tells the Hive Assistant of the workspace's state as it starts.

settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentM.text: The largest file Hive keeps with a card, in bytes: pasted or dropped into the card, attached from an agent's pane, or given by an agent or the Assistant. A larger file is refused, saying so. Files already kept stay.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.attachmentM.note: What the advanced setting "Card attachments: largest file" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in bytes: the largest file Hive keeps with a card (pasted, dropped or attached to it).

settings.advanced.hive.cards.titleNudgeC.text: When an agent or the Hive Assistant gives a card a title longer than this, Hive keeps it and tells the agent a shorter one would be better: a long title is cut in git's history, where it becomes the merge commit's subject, and on the board. The titles you write yourself are never questioned. 0 turns the suggestion off.
settings.advanced.hive.cards.titleNudgeC.note: What the advanced setting "Suggest a shorter title past" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A card title is the one-line name of a card on the task board.

An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in characters ("80 characters"): the length of a card title an agent writes past which Hive suggests a shorter one.

settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..text: Show the text in the developer console: prompts, replies, commands and tools' arguments, under a banner saying it is unredacted, and start each recording with its text box ticked. Tokens, API keys and sign-in details stay masked whatever this says; agents' hive_console stays redacted, and a recording with text is never attached to Copy Diagnostics.
settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..note: What the advanced setting "Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..text: Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text
settings.advanced.hive.console.showText..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.text: A returned review or check copy is used again only once nothing is running in it: no run, no process its check started, its reviewer idle. Past this many minutes, a check waiting for a copy says which copy is still in use and by what. Hive never resets a copy something is still running in.
settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.note: What the advanced setting "Copies: wait for one to be free" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.text: Copies: wait for one to be free
settings.advanced.hive.copies.quietWaitM.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A copy is a folder Hive keeps at one revision for a review or an isolated check.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.des.text: A reviewer reads a card's work, and runs its commands, in a review copy: a folder at exactly the revision under review, which nothing else writes, so what it checks is what was submitted. Turned off, reviewers read the builder's folder as before. Isolated checks (hive-progress --check with --isolated) use the same copies either way.
settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.des.note: What the advanced setting "Reviewers review in review copies" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). hive-progress --check and --isolated are a command and its options: keep them as they are.

settings.advanced.hive.copies.review.tit.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A review copy is a folder Hive keeps at the exact revision a reviewer reviews, which nothing else writes.

settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc.text: Draw Hive without the graphics card, for a graphics driver that leaves Hive's window blank, flickering or crashing. Terminals then draw without WebGL. Takes effect when Hive restarts; to start once without it, run Hive with --disable-gpu.
settings.advanced.hive.disableHardwareAc.note: What the advanced setting "Disable hardware acceleration" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). --disable-gpu is a command-line option: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.text: How long the project’s command that chooses a card’s focused tests may run, when it is submitted and at its merge. Past it, the command is ended and no tests count as chosen: the builder then names them itself.
settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.note: What the advanced setting "Focused tests: longest the choice of tests runs" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.text: Focused tests: longest the choice of tests runs
settings.advanced.hive.focused.pickSecon.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds: how long the project's command that chooses a card's focused tests may run, when the card is submitted and at its merge.

settings.advanced.hive.guidance.desc.text: With Hive's tools, each project agent gets Hive's guidance: how to use the tools, the board and handovers, and its project's latest handover. Claude Code and Copilot get it as the hive server's instructions, Codex after your own developer_instructions. Turned off, agents still get Hive's tools, without the guidance, from their next session. The Hive Assistant always gets its own: they are its role.
settings.advanced.hive.guidance.desc.note: What the advanced setting "Hive's guidance for agents" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Claude Code, Copilot and Codex are CLIs' names, hive the name of Hive's MCP server and developer_instructions a Codex setting: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.guidance.title.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the instructions Hive gives project agents on how to work with it.

settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.text: When Hive's main process nears its memory limit, it writes a snapshot of its memory to the heap folder in Hive's profile before it closes, to find out what filled it. A snapshot can be several gigabytes, holds whatever Hive had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stays on this PC; Hive keeps the newest two. Takes effect when Hive restarts.
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.note: What the advanced setting "Save a memory snapshot if Hive is about to run out of memory" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.text: Save a memory snapshot if Hive is about to run out of memory
settings.advanced.hive.heapSnapshotNearL.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.hooks.missingSeco.text: How long an agent's CLI may go without a hook, from its start (a CLI that sends one then) or from a prompt it went to work on, before Hive says its hooks aren't arriving and shows its status as unknown (#1336). A long think after a prompt's hook never counts. Raise it if a slow machine shows that notice for agents that are fine.
settings.advanced.hive.hooks.missingSeco.note: What the advanced setting "Hooks missing: wait" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. Hooks: the calls an agent's coding agent makes to Hive as it works.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.text: When something arrives in a working agent's inbox, Hive tells it at the end of its next tool call, in that tool's reply, so it can read it without stopping. Turned off, a working agent isn't told until its turn ends or it is idle; nothing is lost, as it stays in the inbox. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.note: What the advanced setting "Tell a working agent at the end of a tool" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Project Settings → Sessions names a section of the project's settings: use its name as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.text: Tell a working agent at the end of a tool
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.checkpoints.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive tells a busy agent what has arrived in its inbox each time one of its tool calls ends.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.d.text: When something arrives in an idle agent's inbox, Hive types one short line into its terminal saying so, which wakes it. Card loops' wakes (the workflow option Wake reviewers and builders) and card watches' are such wakes. Turned off, nothing is typed for anything waiting: it stays in the inbox, the agent's pane shows how many, and its Deliver Now types the line once. A card started on an agent, or a task given to it now, is still typed. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.d.note: What the advanced setting "Wake an idle agent" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Wake reviewers and builders names a workflow option and Project Settings → Sessions a section, Deliver Now a menu item: use their names as Hive shows them.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.idleWakes.t.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive types a short line into an idle agent's terminal to tell it something has arrived in its inbox.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.text: When an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Hive keeps it going to read them first, once a turn: Codex and Copilot by holding their stop back, Claude Code by adding a line to its stop. Turned off, the turn ends as the CLI ends it, and the items wait in the inbox for an idle wake. A project can set its own in Project Settings → Sessions.
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.note: What the advanced setting "Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Codex, Copilot and Claude Code are CLIs' names: keep them. Project Settings → Sessions names a section of the project's settings: use its name as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.text: Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items
settings.advanced.hive.inbox.stopContinu.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: when an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Hive makes it carry on and read them.

settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.de.text: When Hive's own installer is built from its source code (npm run dist, or npm run release), Hive writes the build into the Hive Assistant's journal as its own entry: the version, the commit, what kind of build it was and where the installer is. Only a successful build is written, and only while the journal is on with events in its scope. Turned off, builds aren't written, and a build left for Hive while it was closed is dropped when the workspace opens.
settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.de.note: What the advanced setting "Record builds in the journal" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). npm run dist and npm run release are commands: keep them as they are.

settings.advanced.hive.journal.builds.ti.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The journal is the Hive Assistant's record of decisions and events; builds are installers made from Hive's own source code.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.text: How long, from a lane's end, Hive waits for its builder to finish its turn and read that the lane is finished. Past it, Hive ends the builder's CLI anyway: with its exit command, or killed when that can't be typed (your draft is in its prompt) or doesn't end it.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: longest a lane's end waits for its builder" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.text: Lanes: longest a lane's end waits for its builder
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.endWaitMinu.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.text: A lane starts its agents in new conversations. One that is busy as the lane starts (in a turn, or reading a message Hive just gave it) is started once it is free, for up to this long. After that Hive stops trying: the lane's row says so, and you retry it there or end the lane. Hive never interrupts a turn for it, and never gives the lane's cards to the old conversation.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: longest Hive waits to start a busy agent afresh" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.text: Lanes: longest Hive waits to start a busy agent afresh
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.freshStartW.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("10 min"). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.d.text: When a lane's last card merges (or the lane is abandoned), Hive waits for its builder's turn to end, tells it the lane is finished with each card's merge commit, then ends its CLI with the CLI's own exit command, killing it only if it doesn't exit. Its slot stays its until then. Turned off, Hive stops the builder's session as soon as it is first idle, as before.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.d.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop; a slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.t.text: Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.gentleEnd.t.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.text: When the Hive Assistant may control agents (Settings → Assistant → Control) and is about to end its turn while lanes are running and no watch of its covers them, Hive keeps it going once to say so, naming the lanes' builders, so it watches them before it finishes. At Look and advise the lanes are yours to run, and it isn't told. Turned off, its turn ends as its CLI ends it, and nothing wakes it about those lanes until it watches them again.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop; a watch is what wakes an agent when the cards or lanes it follows change.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.text: Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.unwatchedNo.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn; the Assistant is the Hive Assistant.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.text: After how long a lane whose card waits in Review with nobody reviewing it has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every review; too long, a card can sit unreviewed.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: a long wait for a reviewer" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.text: Lanes: a long wait for a reviewer
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitReviewe.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.text: After how long a lane waiting for you (a request in For you, or a card at its round limit) has its wait marked in the Progress panel's Lanes. Too short marks every wait; too long, a lane can sit unnoticed.
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.note: What the advanced setting "Lanes: a long wait for you" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.text: Lanes: a long wait for you
settings.advanced.hive.lanes.waitYouMinu.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.lostLine.steadySe.text: A line Hive typed into an agent that its CLI didn't take, gone from its input since (a screen of the CLI's took it): how long its input must stay empty, at its prompt, with nothing taken, before Hive types it again or, with nothing to type again, tells you. Raise it if a slow machine has a line typed twice.
settings.advanced.hive.lostLine.steadySe.note: What the advanced setting "Lost line: wait" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced, HI-1959).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. A line: a message Hive typed into an agent's terminal.

settings.advanced.hive.mcp.connectSecond.text: How long Hive waits, once an agent is ready, for its CLI to connect Hive's tools before it tells the agent of new work anyway. A resumed session can be ready before its tools are, and a message then is a turn spent without them (#865). Lower it if messages reach agents late when their CLI doesn't connect Hive's tools.
settings.advanced.hive.mcp.connectSecond.note: What the advanced setting "hive tools: wait to connect" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.mcp.replySeconds..text: How long the hive MCP server waits for Hive to answer one of its tools (a wait's own time comes on top). Raise it when a slow or very busy machine makes hive tools fail with "Hive didn't reply within 300 s" (#371).
settings.advanced.hive.mcp.replySeconds..note: What the advanced setting "hive tools: reply timeout" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.downlo.text: How long Install and Update wait for a catalogue server's zip, redirects included, before they stop with nothing installed. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.downlo.note: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: downloading a server" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.fetchS.text: How long the MCP view waits for a catalogue's list, redirects included, before it shows that catalogue couldn't be read. Raise it on a slow connection.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.fetchS.note: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: reading one" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds. An MCP catalogue is a list of servers to install (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.text: How long each check of this PC for a catalogue server's requirements (its Windows edition and build, Node.js, Docker) may take before it shows as not checked.
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.note: What the advanced setting "MCP catalogues: checking this PC’s requirements" is for (Settings → Advanced, HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.text: MCP catalogues: checking this PC's requirements
settings.advanced.hive.mcpCatalog.probeS.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds (HI-545).

settings.advanced.hive.merge.lockWaitSec.text: How long a merge, or another change to a repository's branches (a pull, switching branch, moving an agent's branch), waits while another Hive on this computer is merging into the same repository. After it, nothing is changed and Hive says which Hive holds the repository: try again once it has finished. Hive never takes the repository from a Hive that is still running.
settings.advanced.hive.merge.lockWaitSec.note: What the advanced setting "Merges: wait for another Hive" is for, and what happens when the wait ends (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Another Hive: the installed Hive and a dev or test Hive on the same machine.

settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.text: In a project without version control, Hive reads the project's files in the background when a card starts, when it is submitted, and when a check of it starts and ends, to find what changed outside the card's files. A read that takes longer than this is stopped: the card starts or is submitted without that list, and the check doesn't count.
settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.note: What the advanced setting "No version control: longest read of the project" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.text: No version control: longest read of the project
settings.advanced.hive.none.baselineSeco.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds ("120 s"). In a project without version control, Hive reads every file of the project in the background when a card starts.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.deliverWork.text: Each agent and the Hive Assistant get the shared note Workspace notes in their instructions when they start, on every CLI and in whichever folder they work: notes about this machine that no committed file should hold. A project's agents get the parts for everyone and their own project's section. Turned off, or with the note empty, nothing is added, from each agent's next session.
settings.advanced.hive.notes.deliverWork.note: What the advanced setting "Deliver workspace notes to agents" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Workspace notes is the name of a shared note: keep it in English, as the Notes view shows it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: Hive gives every agent the shared note Workspace notes when it starts.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.text: How much of the shared note Workspace notes an agent's instructions get, at most, in bytes. A longer note is cut, and agents are told to read the note for the rest. Every agent reads it at every start, so a short note costs less.
settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.note: What the advanced setting "Workspace notes: most an agent gets" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Workspace notes is the name of a shared note: keep it in English, as the Notes view shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.text: Workspace notes: most an agent gets
settings.advanced.hive.notes.workspaceNo.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in bytes: how much of the shared note Workspace notes an agent's instructions get at most.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.text: How long after the turn ends Hive first checks the connection. Each check that finds it still down doubles the wait before the next, up to the longest wait below.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: first check after" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.text: Resuming after a connection drops: first check after
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkFirst.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("30 s").

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.text: The longest Hive waits between two checks of the connection.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: longest wait between checks" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.text: Resuming after a connection drops: longest wait between checks
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkMostS.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("300 s").

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: The address Hive asks to see whether Claude Code's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too. An agent on a server connection is checked at its server's address instead.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Claude Code" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Claude Code
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Claude Code is a product name.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: The address Hive asks to see whether Codex's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Codex" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for Codex
