settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Codex is a product name.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: The address Hive asks to see whether GitHub Copilot's connection is back: its API host. Any reply counts, an error page too.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for GitHub Copilot" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.text: Resuming after a connection drops: address checked for GitHub Copilot
settings.advanced.hive.outage.checkUrl.c.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. GitHub Copilot is a product name.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.text: A failed turn whose error this regular expression finds is never resumed, whatever a CLI's connection error pattern finds: a usage or rate limit, a sign-in, an overloaded server. Resuming wouldn't help those, and could repeat.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: errors that are never a dropped connection" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.text: Resuming after a connection drops: errors that are never a dropped connection
settings.advanced.hive.outage.notConnect.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.des.text: When an agent's turn ends because its CLI couldn't reach its API (a router restarting, Wi-Fi dropping), Hive shows it waiting for the connection, checks the CLI's API host now and then, and once it answers tells the agent to rerun what was cut off and carry on. Never for a usage limit, an expired sign-in or an overloaded server. After three resumes in an hour that end the same way, or once the wait's limit passes, Hive stops and says what to try.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.des.note: What the advanced setting "Resume agents after a connection drops" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.tit.text: Resume agents after a connection drops
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resume.tit.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.text: How many times in an hour Hive resumes the same agent. Once its turn ends on a connection error again after that many, Hive stops: the PC's own network may not have recovered.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: resumes in an hour" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.text: Resuming after a connection drops: resumes in an hour
settings.advanced.hive.outage.resumesPer.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by a number.

settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.text: How long Hive waits for the connection to come back before it stops waiting and tells you.
settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a connection drops: wait at most" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.text: Resuming after a connection drops: wait at most
settings.advanced.hive.outage.waitMinute.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in minutes ("120 min").

settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.text: When a process an agent's command started is still running ten minutes on with the shell that started it gone, Hive says so once in a notice, and tells the agent once at its next tool call or turn's end, so it can end it. Turned off, neither is told; Activity still lists the process as left running, with End It.
settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.note: What the advanced setting "Processes left running: tell me and the agent" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Activity is a tab of Hive's; End It is its button.

settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.text: Processes left running: tell me and the agent
settings.advanced.hive.processes.orphanN.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: a process an agent's command left running, its shell gone, is told in a notice and to the agent.

settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho.text: How many card-loop lanes the Progress panel shows before its lanes scroll, until you drag the section's top edge (the drag is kept per workspace). A workspace that runs many lanes at once can set its own.
settings.advanced.hive.progress.lanesSho.note: What the advanced setting "Progress panel: lanes shown" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.progress.replySec.text: How long hive-progress waits for Hive to answer before a command or a check starts, and for its start to be taken. A check needs the answer (its command is the project's): with none, it asks once more, then runs nothing and says Hive is slow. Raise it when a busy Hive makes checks fail with "Hive is slow to answer" (HI-1892). Kept at 2 minutes at most.
settings.advanced.hive.progress.replySec.note: What the advanced setting "hive-progress: Hive's reply time" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. hive-progress is the command agents run long commands and checks through: keep it as it is.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.de.text: Hive puts each prompt it types into an agent (a message, a wake, a card's start) on one line: runs of spaces become one, line breaks become spaces, and control characters are left out. Turned on, Claude Code and Copilot get the text as written, spacing and line breaks included. Codex, and a slash command in any CLI, still get each line break and tab as a space: Hive types those key by key, where a line break would send the prompt early and a tab complete a word. For Codex, Typed prompts: line breaks (under Codex) can press a new-line key instead. Other control characters are left out either way: they would press keys.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.de.note: What the advanced setting "Send prompts as typed" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Claude Code, Copilot and Codex are CLIs' names: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.asTyped.ti.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the prompts Hive itself types into agents' CLIs.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.text: Before Hive types a prompt or Compact into an agent's CLI, it presses Ctrl+U, which clears what is in the CLI's input, and it presses it again to take back a prompt it stopped part-way. Turned off, Hive never presses it: text left in the CLI's input stays in front of what Hive types and is sent with it, a prompt stopped part-way stays in the input, and Compact can fail behind a draft. Changing Codex's mode still clears its input first, as its menu needs.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.note: What the advanced setting "Clear the CLI's draft before Hive types" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ctrl+U names keys: use the key names your language uses. Compact is a command's name: use it as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.text: Clear the CLI's draft before Hive types
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.clearDraft.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The draft is text left in the input of an agent's CLI, not sent yet.

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.text: When a card is started on an agent, Hive gives it the card wrapped in its own words: which card it is on the board, what it depends on and which docs to read first, and which skill to follow. Turned on, the agent gets only the card's title and description, and what you wrote when you started it. Hive's other prompts (its wakes and messages) stay as they are: they are how Hive and its agents talk.
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.note: What the advanced setting "A card's start in its own words" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive).

settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.text: A card's start in its own words
settings.advanced.hive.prompt.rawCardSta.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what Hive types into an agent when a card is started on it.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.text: How long the merge queue lets one merge check or install run before it ends it. A check ended this way is a failure of the environment, not of the work: the card comes back marked so, and its builder can send the same revision back into the queue. Raise it when a project’s checks really take longer; too long, and a hung check holds the queue up that long.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.note: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: longest a merge check runs" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.text: Merge queue: longest a merge check runs
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkMinute.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("90 min"). A merge check is a command (tests, a build) Hive runs on a card's merged result before it moves the target.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.note: A choice of the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch": ask the user (For you) before each update of the folder.
A choice of the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch": update the folder without asking.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.text: When the branch the merge queue merges into is checked out in a folder (the project folder's main, say), merging changes that folder's files too. Ask each time waits, once a card is tested and ready, for you to approve updating the folder in For you. Automatically updates it at once. Either way the queue first checks that no agent is working in the folder, that it is on that branch and that you have no changes in the files the merge changes, and pauses if not. One rare race, another program switching that folder's branch in the same instant, can leave the merged files in the other branch; Hive then says so and lists them. A branch checked out nowhere is always merged at once.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.note: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ask each time and Automatically are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows. For you is a place in Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.text: Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch
settings.advanced.hive.queue.checkedOutT.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what the merge queue does when the branch it merges into (main, say) is checked out in a folder, usually the project folder, whose files then change.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.text: How many tests at once the merge queue’s run of a card’s focused tests may use, passed to the project’s command that runs them. More finishes sooner but loads the computer, which agents and your own work share.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.note: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: focused tests run at once" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.text: Merge queue: focused tests run at once
settings.advanced.hive.queue.focusedJobs.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by a number: how many of a card's focused tests (the tests its change needs) the merge queue runs in parallel.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.text: A failed merge check whose last 40 lines of output this regular expression finds failed for the network, not the work: the card is returned to its builder marked temporary, and the builder may submit the same revision again (at most twice in a row) instead of a new one. The default finds Node's and npm's network error codes (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT). A project's check can also say so itself by exiting with code 75. (?!) finds nothing: then only a check that couldn't start, ran out of time or was ended counts as temporary.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.note: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: network errors that count as temporary" does (Settings → Advanced). The error codes, (?!) and 75 are literal: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.text: Merge queue: network errors that count as temporary
settings.advanced.hive.queue.networkCode.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The merge queue tests a card's work before merging it; a check that fails for the network, not the work, lets the card's builder submit the same revision again.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.text: When a repository signs its commits, how long the merge queue waits for its merge commit, hooks included, before it takes the signer to be waiting for a passphrase. It then ends the commit, changes nothing in the target and pauses the queue with “signing waits for you”. Raise it when signing or the repository’s commit hooks really take longer; too long, and a signer waiting for you holds the queue up that long.
settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.note: What the advanced setting "Merge queue: longest a signed merge commit takes" does, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced). “signing waits for you” is how the queue’s pause reads.

settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.text: Merge queue: longest a signed merge commit takes
settings.advanced.hive.queue.signSeconds.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in seconds ("60 s"). The merge commit is the commit Hive's merge queue makes when it merges a card; signed means the repository is set to sign commits (GPG or SSH).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.text: How long a capture waits after its trigger before it is saved, so it holds what followed too: what the CLI did next.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: wait after a trigger" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.text: Flight recorder: wait after a trigger
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.afterSec.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("10 s").

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des.text: How many captures Hive keeps in its console-recordings folder: past it, the oldest go. Recordings you made in the developer console are never removed.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.keep.des.note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: captures kept" does (Settings → Advanced). console-recordings is a folder name: keep it.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..text: How long after a capture the same trigger waits before it captures the same agent again, so something that keeps happening saves one capture, not many.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..text: Flight recorder: one capture per trigger and agent every
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.minutes..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in minutes ("10 min").

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.pattern..text: Save a capture when an agent's developer console event has a name or summary this regular expression finds (case-insensitive). The default, (?!), never finds anything: it is off.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.pattern..note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture events matching" does (Settings → Advanced). (?!) is a regular expression: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar.text: Save a capture when a model's safeguards stop a response or switch the model: the agent's newest developer console events, redacted, in Hive's console-recordings folder, with a notice. With any flight recorder trigger on, Hive keeps each agent's newest developer console events in memory (redacted), whether a console is open or not.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.safeguar.note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture safeguard stops" does (Settings → Advanced). console-recordings is a folder name: keep it.
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..text: Save a capture when an agent working on a turn goes silent past its limit, so Hive can't tell what it is doing.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..text: Flight recorder: capture an agent gone silent
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.stalled..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..text: Save a capture when a CLI sends a hook or a status line with a field Hive doesn't know: often the first sign that a CLI update changed something.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI" does (Settings → Advanced). A hook and a status line are what a CLI sends Hive as it works.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..text: Flight recorder: capture something unknown from a CLI
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.unknown..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..text: Save a capture when an agent starts on a version of its CLI other than the one the last agent of that CLI started on.
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..note: What the advanced setting "Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..text: Flight recorder: capture a CLI version change
settings.advanced.hive.recorder.version..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive. The flight recorder saves the developer console's recent events when something rare happens.

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeAft.text: When Hive restarts for an update (Restart to Update, or an installer closing it), the agents that were working, watching their cards or in a card loop start again in their conversations, one at a time, each told where it was. Off: Hive offers to resume them instead, as it does after you quit.
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeAft.note: What the advanced setting "Resume agents after an update" does (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.text: How long an agent Hive resumes after a restart has to be ready. One that isn't is stopped and listed as not resumed, and the next one starts.
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.note: What the advanced setting "Resuming after a restart: ready within" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.text: Resuming after a restart: ready within
settings.advanced.hive.restart.resumeRea.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("90 s").

settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.text: How long an agent's coding agent may keep waiting to retry its model request (rate-limited, or its service unreachable) in one turn before Hive tells the Hive Assistant, once a turn. 0: never.
settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.note: What the advanced setting "Retry wait: tell the Assistant after" does (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.text: Retry wait: tell the Assistant after
settings.advanced.hive.retry.tellAssista.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), followed by its value in seconds ("300 s"). A retry wait: an agent's coding agent waiting to try its model request again.

settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.text: Hive starts each session with TERM=xterm-256color, as its terminal is, and without Windows Terminal's WT_SESSION, so the CLIs draw the same whether Hive was opened from the Start menu or a terminal (Claude Code draws ❯ rather than >). A TERM in your own environment or the session's is kept. Turned off, sessions get the environment Hive was opened with.
settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.note: What the advanced setting "Sessions say their terminal is xterm-256color" does (Settings → Advanced). TERM, WT_SESSION and xterm-256color are names: keep them; ❯ and > are the characters Claude Code draws as its prompt mark.

settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.text: Sessions say their terminal is xterm-256color
settings.advanced.hive.sessions.terminal.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. xterm-256color is a terminal type's name and TERM an environment variable's: keep them.

settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat.text: Show Help → Developer Console (Ctrl+Alt+J): what each CLI sends Hive, next to what Hive made of it.
settings.advanced.hive.showDeveloperFeat.note: What the advanced setting "Show developer features" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.text: Codex and Copilot read Hive's skills from copies Hive puts in each agent's folder (.agents/skills/hive-…); Claude Code gets them at each launch and leaves nothing behind. Once the last of Hive's agents in a folder stops, Hive can remove its copies, so a CLI you run there yourself doesn't see them. Slots only removes them from slots and agents' worktrees, never the project folder. Everywhere removes them from the project folder too. Never keeps them. Only copies Hive made, and nobody changed since, are removed: never your own skills.
settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.note: What the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Codex, Copilot and Claude Code are CLIs' names and .agents/skills/hive-… a folder: keep them. Slots only, Everywhere and Never are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": in the project folder too.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": copies stay, as before.
A choice of the advanced setting "Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder": in every folder but the project folder.

settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.text: Remove Hive's skill copies when no agent works in the folder
settings.advanced.hive.skills.removeIdle.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: the copies of Hive's skills it puts in a folder for Codex and Copilot.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.text: Each card built in a slot works on a branch of its own, such as hive/AM/AM-12-fix-the-login. Once the card is Done and its target branch contains the branch's work (a squash merge too), Hive deletes the branch and notes it on the card. A branch with work that isn't merged, or checked out somewhere, is never deleted. Turned off, the branches stay.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.note: What the advanced setting "Delete a card's branch once it's merged" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane. Keep hive/AM/AM-12-fix-the-login as it is (an example branch name).

settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.text: Delete a card's branch once it's merged
settings.advanced.hive.slots.deleteMerge.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Each card built in a slot (a worktree Hive lends) gets a branch of its own.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..text: A project keeps as many slots as it has builders. A free slot beyond that, unused for a day, is removed: its archive command runs first, and it is kept if that fails. Hive never removes one with an agent or a process in it, a lease, a merge in flight, or work that isn't committed and merged. Turned off, idle slots stay until you remove them.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..note: What the advanced setting "Remove idle slots after a day" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane; a lease is one loan of it.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..text: Remove idle slots after a day
settings.advanced.hive.slots.removeIdle..note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane and gets back when it ends; free ones are kept ready.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.text: At the upgrade to 1.0 your agents' worktrees became slots, keeping their folders (hb2). Once one is free, with no agent or process in it, Hive renames its folder to a slot's name (slot-c), moving its cards' work and the agents' conversations with it, so a slot named after one agent isn't lent to another. Turned off, they keep their names.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.note: What the advanced setting "Rename adopted worktrees to slot names" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane. Keep hb2 and slot-c as they are (folder names).

settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.text: Rename adopted worktrees to slot names
settings.advanced.hive.slots.renameAdopt.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. At the upgrade to 1.0, agents' own worktrees became slots (worktrees Hive lends to a card or a lane), keeping their folder names.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.text: How long Hive lets a slot's setup command, a dependency install or its archive command run before it ends it. A slot whose setup was ended this way isn't lent until it is set up again; an archive command ended so keeps its slot.
settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.note: What the advanced setting "Slots: longest a setup command runs" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.text: Slots: longest a setup command runs
settings.advanced.hive.slots.setupMinute.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in minutes ("60 min"). A slot is a worktree Hive lends to a card or a lane.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.text: In an agent's pane, Hive's own shortcuts (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts) take their keys, apart from those the CLI uses itself. Turned on, every key goes to the CLI, except the command palette's shortcut (Show All Commands), which stays Hive's so every command is still in reach. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V have their own setting.
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.note: What the advanced setting "All keys go to the CLI" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Show All Commands is a command's name and Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts a place in Hive: use them as Hive shows them. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.text: All keys go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.allKeysT.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: every key pressed in an agent's pane goes to its CLI.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.text: In an agent's pane, Ctrl+C copies the terminal's selection (with nothing selected it goes to the CLI, which stops what it is doing), and Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard's text, or a screenshot as an attachment. Turned on, both keys go to the CLI, as in any other terminal: copy and paste with right-click instead, unless right-click goes to the CLI too (a setting under each CLI).
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.note: What the advanced setting "Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys: use the key names your language uses.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.text: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.ctrlCVTo.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V name keys: use the key names your language uses.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.al.note: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": take the text at once.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.as.note: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": show the user the text and ask first.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.bl.note: A choice of the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard": take none.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.de.text: An agent's CLI can put text on the clipboard (OSC 52) just after you press a key or click in its pane, as Copilot does when you copy its own selection. Allow takes it at once; Ask each time shows you the text first, to copy or not; Block takes none. A CLI can never read the clipboard, whatever this says.
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.de.note: What the advanced setting "A CLI putting text on the clipboard" does (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). OSC 52 is the name of a terminal feature: keep it. Allow, Ask each time and Block are the setting's choices: use the words its list shows.

settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.ti.text: A CLI putting text on the clipboard
settings.advanced.hive.terminal.osc52.ti.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive: what Hive does when an agent's CLI asks to set the clipboard (OSC 52).

settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.text: How long the usage history keeps when each request happened, to the second, after a session ends. Past it, a session's use over time is kept in 1-hour steps, so the history stays small. Totals, tokens and costs stay exact; only where a card's or lane's share began or ended inside an hour is less exact, for sessions that old.
settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.note: What the advanced setting "Usage history: keep full detail for" does, and what is lost past it (Settings → Advanced, under Hive). A lane is a card loop: a builder and a reviewer taking cards in turn.

settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.text: Usage history: keep full detail for
settings.advanced.hive.usage.timelineDet.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive, followed by its value in days ("14 days"). The usage history is the record Hive keeps of what each session used.

settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec.text: The longest hive_wait_for_agents waits for agents to finish before it answers. Kept a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout, as card waits are.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.agentsMaxSec.note: What the advanced setting "Agent waits: longest" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon.text: The longest an agent's hive_wait_for_tasks call (without wake) waits before it answers. It has to stay under the CLIs' own tool timeouts, so Hive keeps it a minute below Codex's hive tool timeout whatever is set here.
settings.advanced.hive.wait.cardMaxSecon.note: What the advanced setting "Card waits: longest" is for, and what goes wrong when it is wrong (Settings → Advanced).
An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under its CLI or Hive.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.enforce..text: Hive keeps each project's workflow rules as cards move: what its Version Control options ask for before a card reaches Review, Approved or Done, and what follows when Hive sees a card's work merged or changed outside Hive. Turned off, every rule is off at once in every project: cards move wherever they are put, nothing is refused or asked, and Hive only records what happens to each card's work, without moving cards or waking agents for it.
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.enforce..note: What the advanced setting "Workflow rules are enforced" does, and what turning it off does (Settings → Advanced). Version Control is the name of a tab in Project Settings, and Review, Approved and Done are board stages: use them as Hive shows them.

An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. The workflow rules are the checks a card passes as it moves across the board (review, checks, merging), set per project in its Version Control options.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.text: When a card from an agent's own worktree was squashed into its target, the agent's branch still has its commits, so its next card in the lane would include them. On, Hive moves the branch to the target before the next card starts, once the agent is idle, its runs have ended and its worktree is clean, and only when everything on it is in the target: anything else, it asks you under For you. Off, Hive asks you every time: approve to let it move the branch once, or decline and do it yourself. Hive never moves a branch with workflow rules turned off.
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.note: What the advanced setting "Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge" does (Settings → Advanced). For you is the board's list of what waits for the user: use it as Hive shows it.

settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.text: Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge
settings.advanced.hive.workflow.updateAg.note: An advanced setting's title (Settings → Advanced), listed under Hive. A squash merge puts a card's commits into the target as one new commit, so the agent's own branch (in its worktree) still has the old ones; Hive can move the branch to the target before the agent's next card.

settings.advanced.logs.desc.text: Open the folder containing Hive's log files.
settings.advanced.logs.desc.note: What the setting "Logs" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.logs.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Logs" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.miss.field.text: {cli} {version} sent no field "{field}" here (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.field.note: Under an advanced setting whose value no longer reads what the CLI was recorded sending (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {field} and {fields} are field names, as the CLI sends them.

settings.advanced.miss.list.text: {cli} {version} sent {missing}, which this list doesn't have (it sent {fields}). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.list.note: Under an advanced setting listing the fields Hive knows a CLI sends, when the CLI was recorded sending one it leaves out (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {missing} and {fields} are field names, as the CLI sends them.

settings.advanced.miss.text.text: It doesn't find what {cli} {version} showed ("{shown}"). Fine if {cli} has changed since.
settings.advanced.miss.text.note: Under an advanced setting whose value no longer finds what the CLI was recorded showing (Settings → Advanced). {cli} is the CLI's name, {version} its version; {shown} is the CLI's own text, in English.

settings.advanced.reset.desc.text: Restore every setting in Settings to its default, the advanced settings in advanced.json too. Workspaces and projects, and a workspace's own advanced values, are not affected.
settings.advanced.reset.desc.note: What the setting "Reset all settings" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.reset.tip.text: Recent workspaces and window position are kept.
settings.advanced.reset.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Reset all settings" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.showDeveloperFeatures..text: For power users and for developing Hive. The console opens in a window of its own; Hive captures a source only while it is open on it, redacted. Turning this off closes it.
settings.advanced.showDeveloperFeatures..note: The info tip of the setting this (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.takes.boolean.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced). true and false are the values as written in advanced.json: keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.choice.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): one of a few values. {choices} lists them as advanced.json writes them (allow, ask, block): keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.field.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): the name of a field in a CLI's data.

settings.advanced.takes.list.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.takes.number.text: A whole number of {unit, select, s {seconds} lanes {lanes} agents {agents} other {units}}, {min} to {max}.
settings.advanced.takes.number.note: What an advanced setting takes (its info tip in Settings → Advanced). {unit} picks the word; {min} and {max} are numbers, as advanced.json takes them.

settings.advanced.takes.pattern.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.takes.patternFlags.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced). {flags} are a regular expression's flags (such as i): keep them.

settings.advanced.takes.text.note: What an advanced setting takes (Settings → Advanced): text Hive looks for on a CLI's screen, as it is.

settings.advanced.values.desc.text: Details Hive relies on that a CLI update can break (the text of its prompts, the fields it sends), and timeouts and limits for power users. Change one only when something doesn't work, or Hive's notes on a CLI update say to.
settings.advanced.values.desc.note: What the setting "Advanced settings" does, under its title (Settings → Advanced).

settings.advanced.values.tip.text: Each shows its default beside it once changed, and Reset puts the default back. A value that isn't valid is ignored, with a warning, and the default used. They are kept in advanced.json in your Hive profile, which you can also edit by hand (Open advanced.json): Hive reads it again when it changes. A value for a CLI records the CLI version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed. Some take a workspace's own value too.
settings.advanced.values.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Advanced settings" (Settings → Advanced): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.advanced.workspaceProblem.note: Why a workspace's own advanced value isn't used (Settings → Advanced). {problem} is the reason.

settings.advancedRow.tip.text: {takes} null (or Reset) goes back to Hive's default.{cli, select, yes { It is {group}'s: an override records the version it was made for, and is flagged when another version is installed.{tried, select, yes { Hive tries it on what the CLI was recorded sending, and says when it doesn't find that.} other {}}} other {}}
settings.advancedRow.tip.note: More on an advanced setting: {takes} says what it takes; null is the value that resets it (keep it). {cli} is yes for a CLI's value, {group} that CLI's name; {tried} is yes when Hive tries the value on what the CLI sent.

settings.advancedRow.title.note: An advanced setting's title where it is named alone: {group} is Hive or the CLI it belongs to, {title} the setting's own title.

settings.advancedRow.workspaceDesc.text: This workspace's own value; empty uses Settings → Advanced's. {desc}
settings.advancedRow.workspaceDesc.note: What a workspace's own advanced value is. {desc} is the setting's own description.

settings.advancedRow.workspaceTitle.note: An advanced setting's title for the open workspace's own value. {title} is the setting's title.

settings.agent.error.boolean.note: A value that is not a boolean. true and false are the values as written: keep them.

settings.agent.error.choice.note: A value that is none of a select setting's choices. {choices} lists the values as written.

settings.agent.error.colorBad.text: {title}: "{column}" isn't a column with a #rrggbb colour (columns: {columns}).
settings.agent.error.colorBad.note: A board colour for no column, or not a colour. #rrggbb is the colour's form; {columns} the columns' ids.

settings.agent.error.colorsShape.text: {title} takes an object of column → colour, e.g. {example} (columns: {columns}), or null for Hive's.
settings.agent.error.colorsShape.note: Board colours given something other than an object. {example} is JSON and {columns} the columns' ids: code, as written.

settings.agent.error.effort.note: An effort level the picker does not offer for the model. {levels} is settings.agent.takes.effort*.

settings.agent.error.effortType.note: An effort setting given something other than text. {levels} is settings.agent.takes.effort*.

settings.agent.error.fallbackEntry.text: {title}: each entry needs a value (text) and a label.
settings.agent.error.fallbackEntry.note: A fallback list's entry without a value or with a label that isn't text.

settings.agent.error.fallbackShape.text: {title} takes a list of {shape}, or null for Hive's list.
settings.agent.error.fallbackShape.note: A provider's fallback list given something other than a list. {shape} is an entry's JSON fields: code, as written.

settings.agent.error.isAction.text: it is a button, a status or a list
settings.agent.error.isAction.note: Why a setting has no value to set: it is a button, a status or a list (inside settings.agent.error.notSettable's brackets).

settings.agent.error.notNumber.text: {title} takes a number{hasOff, select, yes { (0 for {off})} other {}}{inherit, select, yes {, or null to inherit} other {}}.
settings.agent.error.notNumber.note: A value that isn't a number. {off} is the label 0 stands for (Never); inherit is yes where null inherits Hive's value.

settings.agent.error.notSettable.text: {title} isn't a value that can be set this way ({why}): change it in {path}.
settings.agent.error.notSettable.note: hive_update_setting on a setting with no value the tools set. {why} is settings.agent.error.isAction or why it is read-only; {path} where the user changes it.

settings.agent.error.oneLine.text: {title} takes one line of text (at most {most} characters).
settings.agent.error.oneLine.note: Text too long or with line breaks. {most} is a number as written.

settings.agent.error.priceBad.text: {title}: "{model}" needs input, cachedInput and output (and optionally cacheWrite), each a number from 0.
settings.agent.error.priceBad.note: A model's price missing a field or not a number. input, cachedInput, output and cacheWrite are JSON fields: keep them.

settings.agent.error.pricesShape.text: {title} takes an object of model → {shape} in USD per million tokens, or null for Hive's prices.
settings.agent.error.pricesShape.note: A provider's prices given something other than an object. {shape} is the JSON fields of a price: code, as written.

settings.agent.error.range.text: {title} takes {min} to {max}{hasOff, select, yes {, or 0 for {off}} other {}}.
settings.agent.error.range.note: A number out of range. {min} and {max} are numbers as written; {off} is the label 0 stands for (Never).

settings.agent.error.text.note: A text setting given something other than text.

settings.agent.error.unknownAdvanced.note: An advanced setting this version of Hive has no definition of.

settings.agent.error.workflow.note: A workflow option's value it doesn't take (#1278). {what} is settings.agent.takes.orInherit.

settings.agent.helps.agents.backgroundTa.text: Agents' background tasks (long test runs) count as finished too soon, or a dev server keeps an agent waiting long after its work is done.

settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.desc.note: What the setting "Processes left running" does, under its title (Settings → Agents).

settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.option.note: A choice of the setting "Processes left running" (Settings → Agents).
A choice of the setting "Processes left running" (Settings → Agents).

settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.tip.text: Hive follows every process an agent's session starts, however it was started. Ask: a notification lists them and offers to end them; the agent's pane header shows them until they end or you decide. End them: Hive ends them as the agent stops. Hive never ends a process the agent didn't start, and asks about the ones still running when you quit.
settings.agents.leftoverProcesses.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Processes left running" (Settings → Agents): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.appearance.uiFontSize.desc.note: What the setting "Interface font size" does, under its title (Settings → Appearance).

settings.appearance.uiFontSize.tip.text: View → Zoom In and Zoom Out scale everything, including the terminal.
settings.appearance.uiFontSize.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Interface font size" (Settings → Appearance): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.changeSettings.desc.text: Let the Assistant change Hive's settings when you ask it to, in every workspace. Whatever this says, it can read and explain them.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.desc.note: What the setting "Change settings" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.changeSettings.tip.text: It suggests a setting first and changes one only when you agree. Each change is listed in its panel with the old and new value and an Undo button. It can never change its own Control, permission modes, the Agent API or what Hive runs (CLI paths, extra arguments, setup commands): it tells you where to change those. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.changeSettings.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Change settings" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens..text: Context size, in tokens, at which the Assistant's Compact button and the context count in its footer turn orange. Never: they never do.
settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens..note: What the setting "Highlight Compact over" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).
The Off box of the number setting "Highlight Compact over" (Settings → Assistant): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens..text: The Assistant usually runs a bigger context than your agents, so it has its own threshold (your agents' is Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above). Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript.
settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens..note: The info tip of the setting "Highlight Compact over" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.control.desc.text: What the Assistant may do beyond looking and advising, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.control.desc.note: What the setting "Control" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.option.agents.note: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.option.look.note: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.option.projec.note: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.tip.text: It never removes agents, discards worktrees or deletes projects, and never types into an agent that is working, asking you something or that you just typed in (see Pause after you type). What it does is listed in its panel, where you can undo its changes. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.control.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): its last paragraph. Pause after you type is another setting: keep its name as Hive shows it.

settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.text: Control agents: it can also add agents, change their settings, start and stop them, and give idle ones tasks, when you ask it to. Stopping a busy agent asks you first.
settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.note: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Control agents.

settings.assistant.control.tip.inbox.text: How the Assistant hears of its inbox follows Settings → Advanced's three inbox switches (Tell a working agent at the end of a tool, Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items, Wake an idle agent), Settings' own values: a project's don't apply to it.
settings.assistant.control.tip.inbox.note: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a paragraph on which inbox switches the Assistant follows. The three names in brackets are settings of Settings → Advanced: use their names as Hive shows them.

settings.assistant.control.tip.look.text: Look and advise: it reads and suggests, and you act.
settings.assistant.control.tip.look.note: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Look and advise.

settings.assistant.control.tip.projects.text: Control agents and create projects: also new projects.
settings.assistant.control.tip.projects.note: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Control agents and create projects.

settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc.text: Once you press Enter in the terminal (you sent what you typed), the Assistant may type there at once.
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc.note: What the setting "Enter ends the pause" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.text: Turn this off if you often type a line and then keep writing (e.g. answering a question, then adding more).
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Enter ends the pause" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.desc.text: The Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace: decisions, plans, events and what it learned, recalled a few lines at a time instead of reading a long handover. Hive adds facts: lanes, merges, unexpected closes.
settings.assistant.journal.desc.note: What the setting "Journal" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.journal.tip.text: For this workspace. Turning it off keeps the entries; Delete Journal… removes them. The Assistant's journal tools follow a change at its next start; it is told at once.
settings.assistant.journal.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Journal" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): the Assistant's journal, its memory across sessions.

settings.assistant.mcp.descAdded.text: The workspace's MCP servers added for the Assistant are chosen in its own view (the Hive Assistant on the activity bar), as a project's are in its MCP tab.
settings.assistant.mcp.descAdded.note: What the setting "MCP servers (this workspace)" says, under its title (Settings → Assistant, HI-2059): the servers are added in the Hive Assistant’s view now. "MCP tab" is a place in Hive: keep it as Hive shows it.

settings.assistant.mcp.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): which of the open workspace's MCP servers the Assistant gets. MCP is a protocol's name: keep it.

settings.assistant.mode.desc.text: How the Assistant works in a new conversation (Coordinator, Planner, QA triager, Release manager, or your own), unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.mode.desc.note: What the setting "Default mode" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.mode.tip.text: Modes are Markdown files in each workspace (.hive/modes): edit them, or add your own, in the Hive Assistant view (the crown on the left). The panel switches mode at once, keeping the conversation.
settings.assistant.mode.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Default mode" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.panelSide.desc.text: Which side of the window the Assistant's panel is on, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.panelSide.desc.note: What the setting "Panel side" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.option.left.note: A choice of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.option.righ.note: A choice of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.tip.text: On the left it sits between the project list and your work, which keeps it clear of Windows notifications and other windows at the bottom right. View → Move Assistant Panel… and the panel's ⋯ menu switch it too.
settings.assistant.panelSide.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc.text: The Assistant's watch on an agent or its card hears the first line of what you send that agent from its pane.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc.note: What the setting "Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip.text: So it knows what you told the agent (an answer, a decision) without asking you again, and can record a decision on the card. Only the first line, only to the Assistant of the same workspace, and only when it is watching that agent or its card.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.title.text: Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent

settings.assistant.typingPause.desc.text: Seconds after you type in an agent's terminal before the Assistant may type there (give it a task or hand its work over).
settings.assistant.typingPause.desc.note: What the setting "Pause after you type" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.typingPause.off.note: The Off box of the number setting "Pause after you type" (Settings → Assistant): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.assistant.typingPause.tip.text: The Assistant types a task by clearing the agent's input line (Ctrl+U) and entering it, which would wipe or mix with something you were writing. During the pause it asks you instead.
settings.assistant.typingPause.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Pause after you type" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc.text: Days a card stays in Done before Hive archives it.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc.note: What the setting "Archive Done cards after" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.off.note: The Off box of the number setting "Archive Done cards after" (Settings → Board): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip.text: Counted from when the card last went into Done (or was brought back from the archive), not from its last change. An archived card is kept: the board's Archived list shows it, and you can bring it back. Hive checks when a workspace opens and every hour.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Archive Done cards after" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.board.colors.desc.text: Pick the colour of each column.
settings.board.colors.desc.note: What the setting "Column colours" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.colors.tip.text: The tint on cards is a light mix of the colour with the theme, so it works in light and dark themes. Reset puts back the default.
settings.board.colors.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Column colours" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.board.columnColors.desc.text: Give each column's heading its colour and tint its cards with it.
settings.board.columnColors.desc.note: What the setting "Colour columns" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.columnColors.tip.text: A card takes the colour of the column it is in. Blocked, stalled and finished cards keep their red, amber and green edge, and their text, over the tint.
settings.board.columnColors.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Colour columns" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.closeToTray.desc.text: Closing the window keeps Hive running in the system tray so sessions continue.
settings.general.closeToTray.desc.note: What the setting "Close to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.closeToTray.tip.text: When off, closing the window quits Hive (asking first if sessions are running). Use File → Exit or the tray menu to quit.
settings.general.closeToTray.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Close to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.commands.desc.text: Your own commands for Hive as a whole: run one by hand (here, or Run Command in the command palette), or pick them for When Hive quits, run, or for any workspace's open and close.
settings.general.commands.desc.note: What the setting "Commands" does, under its title (Settings → General, HI-1954). When Hive quits, run is another setting's title: use its translation.

settings.general.commands.tip.text: Saved in Hive's own settings, never in a workspace, so a repository you clone brings none that run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.commands.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Commands" (Settings → General, HI-1954).

settings.general.commands.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → General): the user's own named commands for Hive as a whole (HI-1954).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.text: When to ask before quitting stops running sessions.
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.note: What the setting "Confirm before quitting" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.al.note: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.ne.note: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.wo.note: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.text: Quitting stops every running session. Their conversations are kept and can be resumed, so by default Hive only asks when an agent is in the middle of something (working, or waiting for your answer).
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.dateFormat.desc.text: How dates show in Hive: sessions named by when they started, the session lists and their tooltips, exports.
settings.general.dateFormat.desc.note: What the setting "Date format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.dmy.note: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.mdy.note: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.syste.note: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.ymd.note: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.tip.text: System uses your Windows language's short date. Names you give sessions stay as you typed them: only the automatic ones (when a session started) follow this. How long ago something happened ("2 hours ago") stays, with the date on hover.
settings.general.dateFormat.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.desc.text: Stop Windows from sleeping while an agent is working or waiting on background tasks, so it doesn't stop mid-task.
settings.general.keepAwake.desc.note: What the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.always.note: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.never.note: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.plugge.note: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.tip.text: Hive lets the PC sleep again as soon as no agent is working. The screen can still turn off and lock. On a laptop, "When plugged in" lets it sleep on battery.
settings.general.keepAwake.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.title.text: Keep the PC awake while agents work

settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.text: Start Hive automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.note: What the setting "Launch at login" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.text: Hive starts hidden in the tray when launched at login.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Launch at login" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.text: Minimising hides Hive to the system tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.note: What the setting "Minimise to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.text: Click the tray icon to bring Hive back.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Minimise to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.onQuit.desc.text: The commands Hive runs, in order, as it quits, once every window's workspace has closed. Hive waits for them, showing them running.
settings.general.onQuit.desc.note: What the setting "When Hive quits, run" does, under its title (Settings → General; HI-1954: a list of the user's commands).

settings.general.onQuit.tip.text: Pick them from Commands above. '{reason}' becomes quit, or update when Hive restarts to install an update (only with that box ticked). Don't wait, in the dialog Hive shows, lets Hive go on while the rest run by themselves. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.general.onQuit.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "When Hive quits, run" (Settings → General; HI-1954). '{reason}' is a placeholder the user writes in a command, and quit and update are the values it becomes: keep all three as they are (the quotes around {reason} keep it from being read as a placeholder of this text). Commands is the title of the setting above; Don't wait is the name of a button of the dialog.

settings.general.onQuit.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → General): a command of the user's that Hive runs as it quits.

settings.general.progressCommands.desc.text: Agents run tests, builds and other commands that take more than about 30 seconds through hive-progress without being asked, so they show in the panel. Off: only when you ask.
settings.general.progressCommands.desc.note: What the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.text: Turn on the Progress panel to use this.
settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.note: Under the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General) while the Progress panel is off.

settings.general.progressCommands.tip.text: hive-progress runs the command unchanged (same output and exit code). Hive's session guidance tells agents to use it, so a change applies to agents started or restarted afterwards. With the Progress panel off, agents aren't told to use it either.
settings.general.progressCommands.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.progressCommands.title.text: Agents show long commands in the Progress panel

settings.general.progressPanel.desc.text: Show long runs agents report, such as tests and builds: how far along each is and the time left, in a panel on the right and on the taskbar button.
settings.general.progressPanel.desc.note: What the setting "Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressPanel.tip.text: Folded, the panel is a strip with a small bar per run; click it, or use Toggle Progress Panel in the command palette. Off hides the panel, the strip and the taskbar progress; agents can still report, and Hive ignores it.
settings.general.progressPanel.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.text: Open the workspace you used last when Hive starts.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.note: What the setting "Reopen last workspace" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.text: Sessions are never resumed automatically — only the workspace is reopened.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Reopen last workspace" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.desc.text: One tip a day about something Hive can do, and a tip at the moments one helps.
settings.general.showTips.desc.note: What the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.showTips.tip.text: Tips show in a small card in the bottom corner and never get in the way. Help → Tips… lists them all, whether this is on or off.
settings.general.showTips.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.title.text: Show a tip when Hive starts

settings.general.startMinimized.desc.text: Start Hive hidden in the system tray.
settings.general.startMinimized.desc.note: What the setting "Start in tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.startMinimized.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Start in tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.timeFormat.desc.text: How times show with the dates.
settings.general.timeFormat.desc.note: What the setting "Time format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.12h.note: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.24h.note: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.tip.text: Applies wherever Hive shows a time, such as a session that started today or the time a screenshot was pasted.
settings.general.timeFormat.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.userName.desc.text: How Hive names you to the Hive Assistant when it tells it you replied to an agent ("Darren replied to B1 on #399").
settings.general.userName.desc.note: What the setting "Your name" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.placeholder.note: The empty box's placeholder of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.tip.text: It goes into the Assistant's conversation, so use whatever form you like it to see. Empty uses "User".
settings.general.userName.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.keybindings.editor.desc.text: Click the pencil (or double-click a shortcut), then press the new keys. Wait a moment after the first combination, or press a second one for a chord such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S.
settings.keybindings.editor.desc.note: What the setting "Shortcuts" does, under its title (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).

settings.keybindings.editor.tip.text: Shortcuts need Ctrl or Alt (or are F-keys). Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Shift+Tab stay with editing and the agents' terminals. Some keys go to the agent while its terminal has focus (for Claude Code: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+G).
settings.keybindings.editor.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Shortcuts" (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.mcpCatalogs.sources.desc.text: Each catalogue is a catalog.json at an https:// or file:// address. Turned off, its servers aren't listed (those installed stay). Hive reads them only when the Catalogue opens or you refresh it, and checks every download against its catalogue.
settings.mcpCatalogs.sources.desc.note: What the setting "Catalogues" does, under its title (Settings → MCP Catalogues, HI-545). Keep catalog.json, https:// and file:// as they are.

settings.mcpCatalogs.sources.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → MCP Catalogues, HI-545): the catalogues listed, each on or off.

settings.notifications.bannerPosition.de.text: Where notifications and tips pop up in the window.
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.de.note: What the setting "Pop-up position" does, under its title (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.bannerPosition.op.note: A choice of the setting "Pop-up position" (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.bannerPosition.ti.text: Several stack, the newest nearest the edge. Bottom right stays left of the Assistant's panel.
settings.notifications.bannerPosition.ti.note: The info tip of the setting "Pop-up position" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.bannerScope.desc.text: Which agents, lanes and cards the window you are using pops up a notification about.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.desc.note: What the setting "Show pop-ups about agents for" does, under its title (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.bannerScope.optio.note: A choice of the setting "Show pop-ups about agents for" (Settings → Notifications).
A choice of the setting "Show pop-ups about agents for" (Settings → Notifications, HI-2320): no pop-ups about agents; they are kept under the bell (the Notifications panel).

settings.notifications.bannerScope.tip.text: One left out is kept under the bell without popping up. With Hive in the background, Windows notifications come whatever this says. Clicking one about another window's project brings that window up.
settings.notifications.bannerScope.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Show pop-ups about agents for" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.des.text: How long a pop-up stays, unless it waits for you.
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.des.note: What the setting "Pop-ups close after (seconds)" does, under its title (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.tip.text: One with buttons, or an error, stays at least 15 seconds. It stays while the pointer or the keyboard is on it, and while the window is in the background.
settings.notifications.bannerSeconds.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Pop-ups close after (seconds)" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.desc.text: Play a sound when an agent finishes or needs your input.

settings.notifications.chimeEnabled.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Completion chime" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.notifyOnFinished..note: The info tip of the setting "Notify when an agent finishes" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.d.text: Notify when a session is waiting for permission or input.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.d.note: What the setting "Notify when input is needed" does, under its title (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.t.text: Triggered by the agent's permission prompts and questions.
settings.notifications.notifyOnWaiting.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Notify when input is needed" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.suggestFreshStart.note: The info tip of the setting "Suggest a fresh start" (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.taskbarCount.desc.text: A badge on Hive's taskbar button, and the window title, show how many agents need you.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.desc.note: What the setting "Show a count on the taskbar button" does, under its title (Settings → Notifications).

settings.notifications.taskbarCount.tip.text: The same count as the status bar: agents waiting for your input, and those that finished while you were not looking. Each window shows its own workspace.
settings.notifications.taskbarCount.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Show a count on the taskbar button" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.notifications.waitingBannerStay.text: Until you click or dismiss it, or answer the agent. Off, they close like the others.

settings.notifications.waitingBannerStay.text: Answering the agent anywhere (its terminal, another window) closes its pop-up, and its entry under the bell says Answered.
settings.notifications.waitingBannerStay.note: The info tip of the setting "Pop-ups for an agent waiting for you stay until handled" (Settings → Notifications): more on what it does and when it applies.
