settings.option.inherit.note: A choice of a project's setting: use Hive's own setting (Settings) instead of one of its own.

settings.option.off.note: A choice of a setting that is on or off, beside Inherit or Default.

settings.option.on.note: A choice of a setting that is on or off, beside Inherit or Default.

settings.path.level.note: Where a workflow default is: Settings, its section (Version Control), its part (Hive defaults or Workspace defaults) and its title.

settings.path.project.note: Where a project's setting is: Project Settings, its section and its title.

settings.path.settings.note: Where a setting is: Settings, its section and its title. Settings is the name of the Settings view.

settings.path.versionControl.note: Where a project's workflow option is: the project's Version Control tab, its Workflow section, and the option's title (glossary 2.1).

settings.project.agents.desc.text: The Assistant adds agents up to the project's Maximum agents (Version Control → Workflow), and you can add more yourself, up to {max, number}, each working in the project folder or a slot. Agents without their own settings use this project's.
settings.project.agents.desc.note: What the setting "Agents" does, under its title (Project Settings → Agents). {max} is the most agents a project can have (24).

settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.d.text: Files kept with this project's cards go to the Recycle Bin this long after a card is archived. Open and Done cards keep theirs.
settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.d.note: What the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" does, under its title (Project Settings → Storage).

settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.o.note: A choice of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): 3 days after the card was archived.
A choice of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): 30 days after the card was archived.
A choice of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): 7 days after the card was archived.
A choice of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): 90 days after the card was archived.
A choice of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): archived cards keep their files.

settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.t.text: Hive looks when the workspace opens and once a day. Bringing a card back from the archive in time keeps its files. Afterwards the card says when they were removed, and its links to them show as removed. Cards archived because their project was hidden or removed keep theirs.
settings.project.cardAttachmentCleanup.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Remove archived cards' attachments" (Project Settings → Storage): more on what it does and when it applies.
A setting's title (Project Settings → Storage): when the files kept with this project's archived cards (screenshots, logs) go to the Recycle Bin.

settings.project.chime.desc.text: Play a sound when an agent in this project finishes or needs input.
settings.project.chime.desc.note: What the setting "Completion chime" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.chime.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Completion chime" (Project Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.de.text: Context size (tokens) at which Compact is highlighted for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Suggest compacting above.
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.de.note: What the setting "Suggest compacting above" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.of.note: The Off box of the number setting "Suggest compacting above" (Project Settings → Sessions): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.ti.text: Only changes when the Compact button turns orange; compacting is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.project.compactSuggestTokens.ti.note: The info tip of the setting "Suggest compacting above" (Project Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.desc.text: Hive tells a working agent of what arrives in its inbox at the end of its next tool call. Off: it isn't told until its turn ends or it is idle; nothing is lost.
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.desc.note: What the setting "Tell a working agent at the end of a tool" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.tip.text: Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Tell a working agent at the end of a tool.
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Tell a working agent at the end of a tool" (Project Settings → Sessions). Settings → Advanced names Hive's settings: use its names as Hive shows them.

settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.title.text: Tell a working agent at the end of a tool
settings.project.inboxCheckpoints.title.note: A setting's title (Project Settings → Sessions): Hive tells a busy agent what has arrived in its inbox each time one of its tool calls ends.

settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.desc.text: Hive types a short line into an idle agent's terminal when something arrives in its inbox, card loops' wakes included. Off: nothing is typed for what waits; the agent's pane shows how many, and Deliver Now types the line once.
settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.desc.note: What the setting "Wake an idle agent" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions). Deliver Now is a menu item of the agent's pane: use its name as Hive shows it.

settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.tip.text: A card started on an agent, or a task given to it now, is still typed. Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Wake an idle agent.
settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Wake an idle agent" (Project Settings → Sessions). Settings → Advanced names Hive's settings: use its names as Hive shows them.

settings.project.inboxIdleWakes.title.note: A setting's title (Project Settings → Sessions): Hive types a short line into an idle agent's terminal to tell it something has arrived in its inbox.

settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.d.text: Hive keeps an agent ending its turn with unread items going to read them, once a turn. Off: the turn ends, and they wait in the inbox for an idle wake.
settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.d.note: What the setting "Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.t.text: Codex and Copilot have their stop held back, Claude Code a line added to it. Inherit follows Settings → Advanced → Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items.
settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items" (Project Settings → Sessions). Codex, Copilot and Claude Code are CLIs' names: keep them. Settings → Advanced names Hive's settings: use its names as Hive shows them.

settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.t.text: Keep an agent going when it stops with unread items
settings.project.inboxStopContinuation.t.note: A setting's title (Project Settings → Sessions): when an agent is about to end its turn with items in its inbox it hasn't read, Hive makes it carry on and read them.

settings.project.key.title.note: A setting's title (Project Settings → General): the project's key, 2–4 letters such as AM that its cards are named by (AM-12).

settings.project.keybindings.desc.text: Change one to give this project its own; Reset returns it to the global shortcut. Stored in the project’s .hive folder, which is not committed.
settings.project.keybindings.desc.note: What the setting "Shortcuts" does, under its title (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).

settings.project.keybindings.title.note: A setting's title (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).

settings.project.metadata.desc.text: Stored in the project's .hive/project.json (excluded from git). Changes apply to new sessions; restart a running session to apply them.
settings.project.metadata.desc.note: What the setting "Settings file" does, under its title (Project Settings → Advanced).

settings.project.reset.desc.text: Everything on this page goes back to Inherit. Agents, and skill and MCP opt-outs, are kept.
settings.project.reset.desc.note: What the setting "Reset project settings" does, under its title (Project Settings → Advanced).

settings.project.storage.desc.text: Measured in the background; Refresh measures again. The coding agents’ own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren’t counted, and Clean Up… and Purge… never touch them.
settings.project.storage.desc.note: What the setting "What Hive keeps" does, under its title (Project Settings → Storage). Clean Up… and Purge… are buttons: use their names as translated there.

settings.project.suggestFreshStart.desc.text: A notice when this project's work has finished, with Start Fresh (Idle Agents).
settings.project.suggestFreshStart.desc.note: What the setting "Suggest a fresh start" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions). Start Fresh (Idle Agents) is a command: keep its name as Hive shows it.

settings.project.suggestFreshStart.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Suggest a fresh start" (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.desc.text: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript is flagged for this project. Empty inherits Settings → Sessions → Warn when a transcript is over.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.desc.note: What the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" does, under its title (Project Settings → Sessions).

settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.off.note: The Off box of the number setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Project Settings → Sessions): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.tip.text: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Hive; handing the work over to a new conversation makes it short again.
settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Project Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.project.transcriptWarnMB.title.text: Warn when a transcript is over

settings.project.workflow.platform.desc.text: None or Git, from the next card: Git only where a Git repository is found and no other version control is. Each keeps its own workflow options.
settings.project.workflow.platform.desc.note: What the setting "Version control" does (the project’s Version Control tab): switching applies from the next card; cards started keep their rules. None and Git: glossary 2.1.

settings.project.workflow.platform.git.note: A value of the setting "Version control": Git (glossary 2.1: keep).

settings.project.workflow.platform.none.note: A value of the setting "Version control": no version control (glossary 2.1: None).

settings.project.workflow.platform.title.note: A setting's title (the project's Version Control tab): None or Git (glossary 2.1).

settings.project.worktreeSetup.desc.text: Runs in a new worktree before its agent's first session, e.g. npm install. Its output shows in the agent's pane.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.desc.note: What the setting "Setup command" does, under its title (Project Settings → Agents).

settings.project.worktreeSetup.tip.text: Runs with cmd.exe in the worktree folder. If it fails, the pane offers to retry or to start the agent without it.
settings.project.worktreeSetup.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Setup command" (Project Settings → Agents): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.projectSection.advanced.desc.text: Where the settings are stored, and resetting them.
settings.projectSection.advanced.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Advanced" of Project Settings: what it holds.

settings.projectSection.advanced.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.projectSection.agents.desc.text: The project’s agents and the settings of each CLI they run.
settings.projectSection.agents.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Agents" of Project Settings: what it holds.

settings.projectSection.agents.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left: the project’s agents, with each CLI’s settings under it.

settings.projectSection.general.desc.text: The project’s key, which names its cards, and the provider its new agents use.
settings.projectSection.general.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "General" of Project Settings: what it holds.

settings.projectSection.general.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left: the project’s key and its default provider.

settings.projectSection.keys.desc.text: Shortcuts for project and session commands while this project is selected, over the global ones.
settings.projectSection.keys.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Keyboard Shortcuts" of Project Settings: what it holds.

settings.projectSection.keys.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.projectSection.sessions.desc.text: Compacting and notifications for this project.
settings.projectSection.sessions.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Sessions" of Project Settings: what it holds.

settings.projectSection.sessions.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.projectSection.storage.desc.text: What Hive keeps for this project: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and the agents’ worktrees. Clean Up… moves old backups and attachments to the Recycle Bin; Purge… removes everything Hive keeps for its sessions.
settings.projectSection.storage.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Storage" of Project Settings: what it holds. Clean Up… and Purge… are buttons: use their names as translated there.

settings.projectSection.storage.label.note: A section of Project Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession.text: Let {provider}'s agent view move a session into its own background service. Applies to sessions started afterwards.
settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession.note: What the setting "Allow background sessions" does (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name; its agent view is a screen of that CLI.

settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession.text: Off by default. In {provider}, pressing ← on an empty prompt (easy to do while moving through text) opens its agent view and moves the session into the background. Hive can then no longer see it or stop it: Stop only closes the terminal, the session keeps running, and resuming it fails until it is stopped with "{cli} stop".
settings.provider.allowBackgroundSession.note: The info tip of the setting "Allow background sessions" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name; "{cli} stop" is a command: keep it.
A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.d.text: Compare the installed version with the latest release when Hive starts.
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.d.note: What the setting "Check for updates on launch" does, under its title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.t.text: Hive never updates {provider} without asking. Standalone installs may also update themselves.
settings.provider.checkUpdatesOnLaunch.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Check for updates on launch" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.
A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.costSource.desc.text: Where a session's API-equivalent cost comes from: {provider}'s own report, or your prices in the table below.
settings.provider.costSource.desc.note: What the setting "Session costs" does (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.costSource.option.pric.note: A choice of the setting "Session costs" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.costSource.option.repo.note: A choice of the setting "Session costs" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.costSource.tip.text: {provider}'s reported cost follows its own price table and updates with the CLI; Hive never recomputes it, even when that table lags a price change. Choose your prices for your own rates (a discount, another tier). Either way the table is used for sessions with no reported cost.
settings.provider.costSource.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Session costs" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.costSource.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.effortFallback.desc.text: The effort levels offered when {provider} doesn't report a model's own. With the CLI's answer, each model offers just the levels it takes.
settings.provider.effortFallback.desc.note: What the setting "Effort levels (fallback)" is (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.effortFallback.tip.text: The value is what Hive passes to {provider}; the name is what the pickers and footer show.
settings.provider.effortFallback.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Effort levels (fallback)" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot): its table's two columns. {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.effortFallback.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.co.note: The confirmation before the setting is turned on (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot): its detail.

settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.co.text: Connections will be able to run sessions where {provider} executes every command, file edit and network request without asking.
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.co.note: The confirmation before the setting "Enable the <mode> option" is turned on (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is a coding agent's name.

settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.de.text: Allow connections to choose {choices}, where the agent runs every action without asking.
settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.de.note: What the setting "Enable the <mode> option" does (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {choices} lists the modes' names, in quotes, joined with "or".

settings.provider.enableDangerousMode.qu.note: A mode's name in quotes, in a list of the modes a setting unlocks. Use your language's quotation marks.

If your language puts the names of modes and options in quotation marks, write {quotedNames} in place of {names}: the same list with each name in its own quotation marks.

settings.provider.enabled.desc.note: What the setting "Use <provider>" does (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.enabled.tip.text: When off, {provider} agents stay listed but can't start, and Hive doesn't check for its CLI.
settings.provider.enabled.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Use <provider>" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.enabled.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot): turns the provider on. {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.executablePath.desc.text: Full path to the {provider} CLI ({cli}.exe). Leave empty to detect it automatically.
settings.provider.executablePath.desc.note: What the setting "CLI path" does (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name, {cli} its command: keep it.

settings.provider.executablePath.placeho.note: The empty box's placeholder of the setting "CLI path" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.executablePath.tip.text: Detection checks PATH and the usual install folders. Copies bundled with editor extensions (VS Code, Cursor…) are never used — Hive requires the standalone CLI.
settings.provider.executablePath.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "CLI path" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.provider.executablePath.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.modelFallback.desc.text: Hive asks {provider} which models it has and what each can do. This list is only used when it can't be asked (not installed, too old, or an unexpected answer).
settings.provider.modelFallback.desc.note: What the setting "Models (fallback)" is (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.modelFallback.tip.text: Add, remove and rename models; a custom model ID can still be typed in any model picker. Reset to defaults goes back to Hive's list, which then follows Hive's updates.
settings.provider.modelFallback.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Models (fallback)" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.provider.modelFallback.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.prices.descEstimated.text: Used to estimate what {provider} sessions would cost at API prices (shown with ≈ on the Overview). USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.descEstimated.note: What the setting "API prices" is (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot), for a provider that reports no costs. {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.prices.descReported.text: {provider} reports each session's cost itself; these prices are used for sessions without one, or for all of them with Session costs set to your prices. USD per million tokens.
settings.provider.prices.descReported.note: What the setting "API prices" is (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot), for a provider that reports its costs. {provider} is its name; Session costs is the setting above it.

settings.provider.prices.tip.text: Hive's starting prices are the published ones, checked {checked}: edit any that are out of date, add models and remove them. The table lists the models {provider} has, so a new one shows with "No price" until you enter one. Hive never fetches prices. On a subscription you are not charged these — they show how heavy the work was.
settings.provider.prices.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "API prices" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {checked} is a date; {provider} is its name; "No price" is a badge in the table.

settings.provider.prices.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.provider.status.tip.text: Where Hive found {provider}, whether it is signed in and whether an update is available.
settings.provider.status.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Installation" (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot). {provider} is its name.

settings.provider.status.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → a provider page: Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot).

settings.providers.list.desc.text: Turn on the coding agents you want to use. Agents of a provider that is off stay listed but can't start.
settings.providers.list.desc.note: What the setting "Providers" does, under its title (Settings → Providers).

settings.providers.list.tip.text: Each agent runs the CLI of the connection it chose (Settings → Accounts & Connections). A provider needs its CLI installed.
settings.providers.list.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Providers" (Settings → Providers): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.section.accounts.desc.text: An account is a sign-in Hive keeps (signed in through the CLI's own sign-in) or a server such as DeepSeek or Ollama, reached by its base URL and key. A connection is a setup on an account: its model, effort, context, permission mode and extra arguments. Agents and the Assistant each choose a connection, and every account shares your conversations. Drag accounts into your order: a new agent gets the first connection of the first account that's on here.
settings.section.accounts.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Accounts & Connections" of Settings (HI-2107): what it holds, and what the order of accounts decides.

settings.section.accounts.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left (HI-2107): accounts, the sign-ins and servers Hive's agents reach their models through, and connections, the named setups on them (model, effort, mode) that agents choose.

settings.section.advanced.desc.text: Developer features, the details Hive relies on that a CLI update can break (advanced.json), logs, data and resetting Hive.
settings.section.advanced.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Advanced" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.advanced.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.agentApi.desc.text: Local API and built-in MCP server that let agents interact with Hive.
settings.section.agentApi.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Agent API" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.agentApi.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.agents.desc.text: Defaults for every project’s agents: how long background tasks count, and processes agents leave running.
settings.section.agents.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Agents" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.agents.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left: defaults for every project’s agents.

settings.section.appearance.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Appearance" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.appearance.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.assistant.desc.text: The Hive Assistant's defaults: the side panel's overseer of each workspace (Ctrl+Alt+I). Each workspace can change them in the panel's Assistant Settings.
settings.section.assistant.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Assistant" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.assistant.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.board.desc.text: The task board's colours and housekeeping, the same in every workspace.
settings.section.board.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Board" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.board.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.general.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "General" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.general.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.keybindings.desc.text: Change, remove or add shortcuts for any command. Projects can set their own for project and session commands (Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).
settings.section.keybindings.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Keyboard Shortcuts" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.keybindings.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.mcpCatalogs.desc.text: Where the MCP view's Catalogue finds servers to install. Hive's own comes first; add a company's or a community's list by its address.
settings.section.mcpCatalogs.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "MCP Catalogues" of Settings (HI-545): what it holds.

settings.section.mcpCatalogs.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left (HI-545): the lists of MCP servers to install. MCP is a protocol’s name: keep it.

settings.section.notifications.desc.text: Chimes and desktop notifications when agents finish or need you.
settings.section.notifications.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Notifications" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.notifications.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.provider.desc.text: The {provider} CLI (the standalone one — copies bundled with editor extensions are not used): where it is, its updates, its fallback lists and prices. Models, effort and modes are on connections.
settings.section.provider.desc.note: Under the heading of a provider's page in Settings: what it holds. {provider} is a coding agent's name (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot).

settings.section.providers.desc.text: The coding agents Hive can run. Turn on the ones you use; each has its own page below with its CLI. Models, effort and modes are on connections (Accounts & Connections).
settings.section.providers.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Providers" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.providers.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.sessions.desc.text: Transcript backups, cache estimates and session behaviour.
settings.section.sessions.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Sessions" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.sessions.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.updates.desc.text: Keeping Hive itself up to date. New versions come from Hive's GitHub releases and are verified before they install.
settings.section.updates.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Updates" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.updates.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.section.workflow.desc.text: The workflow options projects start from: Hive defaults, for every workspace, and the open workspace’s over them. A project’s own options, in its Version Control tab, win over both.
settings.section.workflow.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Version Control" of Settings: what it holds. Hive defaults and the Version Control tab: names as Hive shows them (glossary 2.1).

settings.section.workflow.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left: the workflow options projects start from, Hive’s and the open workspace’s (HI-1768). Named as a project’s Version Control tab (glossary 2.1).

settings.section.workspace.desc.text: The open workspace's own: its projects that Hive leaves out (hidden, or removed from Hive with their handovers and cards packed into the folder), how much Hive keeps for each project, and antivirus scanning. Its workflow defaults are in Version Control.
settings.section.workspace.desc.note: Under the heading of the section "Workspace" of Settings: what it holds.

settings.section.workspace.label.note: A section of Settings, in its list on the left.

settings.sessions.backupRetention.desc.text: How long Hive keeps its backups of sessions the CLI still has. After that many days without activity they go to the Recycle Bin. A session whose only copy is Hive's backup is never touched.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.desc.note: What the setting "Keep transcript backups" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.backupRetention.option.note: A choice of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.backupRetention.tip.text: Only Hive's own copies go: the CLI's transcript stays, so the session can still be opened and resumed, and what it used stays in the usage history. To remove sessions whose only copy is Hive's, delete them yourself or use Clean Up in Storage.
settings.sessions.backupRetention.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Keep transcript backups" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.desc.text: Copy each session's transcript into the project's .hive/sessions folder.
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.desc.note: What the setting "Back up transcripts" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.tip.text: Agents delete old transcripts after a while (Claude Code: 30 days by default). Backups let you resume and review sessions later. Archived sessions are always preserved.
settings.sessions.backupTranscripts.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Back up transcripts" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.cacheTtl.desc.text: Used to estimate whether resuming a session needs to re-cache its context.
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.desc.note: What the setting "Prompt cache lifetime" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.cacheTtl.option.1h.note: A choice of the setting "Prompt cache lifetime" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.cacheTtl.option.5m.note: A choice of the setting "Prompt cache lifetime" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.cacheTtl.option.auto.note: A choice of the setting "Prompt cache lifetime" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.cacheTtl.tip.text: Auto detects the cache type from the transcript (5 minutes or 1 hour).
settings.sessions.cacheTtl.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Prompt cache lifetime" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.d.text: Context size, in tokens, at which the context in an agent's pane footer turns orange. Never: it never does.
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.d.note: What the setting "Suggest compacting above" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.o.note: The Off box of the number setting "Suggest compacting above" (Settings → Sessions): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.t.text: Compacting summarises the conversation so every later message is cheaper; the full history stays in the transcript. Projects can set their own value in Project Settings, and the Assistant has its own (Settings → Assistant). Compact is always available once the agent has finished.
settings.sessions.compactSuggestTokens.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Suggest compacting above" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.confirmStop.desc.text: Ask before stopping a running session.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.desc.note: What the setting "Confirm before stopping" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.confirmStop.tip.text: Stopped sessions can always be resumed.
settings.sessions.confirmStop.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Confirm before stopping" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.defaultView.desc.text: How the Session tab shows a project's agents until you choose with its Panes | Tiles toggle.
settings.sessions.defaultView.desc.note: What the setting "Default session view" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions). Panes and Tiles are the toggle's choices: use their translations.

settings.sessions.defaultView.option.pan.note: A choice of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): the agents' terminals in panes. Use the Panes | Tiles toggle's word.

settings.sessions.defaultView.option.til.note: A choice of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): a small tile per agent. Use the Panes | Tiles toggle's word.

settings.sessions.defaultView.tip.text: Panes shows each agent's terminal; Tiles shows each agent as a small tile, so a whole team fits on one screen. A project remembers its own choice once you use its toggle, so changing this only affects projects that haven't chosen yet.
settings.sessions.defaultView.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc.text: The Sessions tab shows new messages of a running session as they arrive.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc.note: What the setting "Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip.text: Off: the transcript shows what was there when you opened it; Refresh loads what is new. You can also switch following on in the viewer itself. The Session tab always shows the agent working.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.titl.text: Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc.text: How the Overview and the session lists update while agents work.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc.note: What the setting "Overview updates" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.option.note: A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip.text: Live updates as sessions change, at most every 15 seconds and only while the tab is shown. Each update reads the project's session files, so with many sessions or agents a slower choice keeps Hive lighter. Refresh always updates at once.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc.text: Count what Hive's Agent API, tools, guidance and skills cost, for the Performance view.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc.note: What the setting "Record performance metrics" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip.text: Only totals are kept: request and reply sizes, times and outcomes, the size of what each session was given, and the providers' own reported usage. Never prompts, replies, tokens or paths. Kept 30 days per workspace in .hive/metrics (git-ignored, this machine's). Turned off, nothing new is recorded; what was recorded stays until you reset it.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Record performance metrics" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc.text: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc.note: What the setting "Reset performance metrics" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip.text: Starts the history again from now. Session usage and transcripts are not affected.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Reset performance metrics" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.text: When Hive closed without quitting (a crash, or it was ended), resume the agents that were running when it starts again.
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.note: What the setting "Resume agents after an unexpected close" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.text: Off: Hive only tells you, with Resume All for you to choose. Either way the notice says when Hive was last seen and which agents were running.
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.note: The info tip of the setting "Resume agents after an unexpected close" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.text: Resume agents after an unexpected close

settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc.text: The order of the agents' tiles in the Tiles view.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc.note: What the setting "Tile order" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.tileOrder.option.panes.note: A choice of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions): the tiles in the panes' order. The default.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.option.urgen.note: A choice of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions): waiting for you and stalled first, then working, then idle.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip.text: Same as panes keeps the agents in their panes' order, so a builder stays beside its reviewer: tiles waiting for you or stalled are highlighted where they are, and a page button counts them on other pages. By urgency puts them first, then the agents working, then the idle ones.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions). "Same as panes" and "By urgency" are its choices: use their translations.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Sessions): the order of the Tiles view's tiles.

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc.text: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript turns orange in its footer and Hive notifies you once.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc.note: What the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.off.note: The Off box of the number setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Settings → Sessions): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip.text: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Hive: each turn, resume and transcript view has more to read. Compacting doesn't shrink the file, which keeps the whole history; handing the work over to a new conversation does (click the size in the footer for Hand Over to…, and choose the agent itself). Projects can set their own value in Project Settings.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.title.text: Warn when a transcript is over

settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc.text: Forget what the cache holds; a transcript it had is read again when it is next needed. The usage history stays.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc.note: What the setting "Clear the usage cache" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip.text: Only needed if a running session's token counts look wrong. Nothing else is lost: sessions, transcripts, backups and the usage history stay as they are.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Clear the usage cache" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc.text: How many transcripts Hive keeps the token use of in memory while it runs, so a running session's figures follow each turn without reading it again.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc.note: What the setting "Usage cache size" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip.text: What each session used is kept in the usage history, in the workspace's .hive folder: this cache only spares reading a transcript again while Hive runs. The least recently used go first when it is full. {min, number} to {max, number}.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Usage cache size" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies. {min} and {max} are the fewest and most transcripts it can be set to.

settings.slotCopy.desc.text: Git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new slot and review copy, comma separated or one per line, such as .env files. Projects inherit it, and can set their own in Version Control → Slots and copies.
settings.slotCopy.desc.note: What the workflow default “Files copied into new slots” does, at Hive’s and a workspace’s level (glossary 2.5: slot, review copy). Keep .env as it is.

settings.slotCopy.title.note: A workflow default (Git) and a project setting: the git-ignored files copied from the project folder into each new slot and review copy (glossary 2.5: slot, review copy).

settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc.text: Look for a new version of Hive shortly after it starts and every 6 hours.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc.note: What the setting "Check for updates automatically" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip.text: When off, Hive only checks when you choose Help → Check for Updates…; development builds never update.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Check for updates automatically" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d.text: Download a new version in the background as soon as it is found.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d.note: What the setting "Download updates automatically" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t.text: When off, the status bar says a new version is available and you choose when to download it. Downloads are checked against the release checksum.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t.note: The info tip of the setting "Download updates automatically" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.install.desc.text: When a downloaded update is installed.
settings.updates.install.desc.note: What the setting "Install updates" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.option.auto.note: A choice of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.option.manual.note: A choice of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.tip.text: Automatically: the update installs when you next quit Hive (never while it is running, so your sessions are not interrupted); Restart and Update installs it straight away. Manually: it installs only when you choose Restart and Update. Either way, Hive asks before stopping agents that are working.
settings.updates.install.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.prerelease.desc.text: Also offer beta versions published before a full release.
settings.updates.prerelease.desc.note: What the setting "Include pre-releases" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.prerelease.tip.text: Pre-releases get new features first and may have rough edges. Turning this off again waits for the next full release rather than going back.
settings.updates.prerelease.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Include pre-releases" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.status.tip.text: The version you are running and the result of the last check.
settings.updates.status.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Hive Desktop version" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.desc.text: For every workspace: what each project starts from unless its workspace or the project sets its own. Pick a preset, or set each option, for None or for Git.
settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.desc.note: What the setting "Hive defaults" is, under its title (Settings → Version Control). None and Git: glossary 2.1.

settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.tip.text: Until 1.0’s settings tidy, Settings → Workflow defaults: nothing set there changed.
settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.tip.note: The info tip of "Hive defaults" (Settings → Version Control): its old place, so a search for its old name finds it. Workflow defaults was the old section’s name: translate it as that section was.

settings.workflow.hiveDefaults.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Version Control): the workflow options every project of every workspace starts from (Darren's words, HI-1768).

settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.desc.text: For this workspace’s projects, over Hive defaults; a project sets its own in its Version Control tab.
settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.desc.note: What the setting "Workspace defaults" is, under its title (Settings → Version Control). Hive defaults and the Version Control tab: names as Hive shows them.

settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.tip.text: Until 1.0’s settings tidy, the workflow defaults in Settings → Workspace: nothing set there changed.
settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.tip.note: The info tip of "Workspace defaults" (Settings → Version Control): its old place, so a search for it finds it.

settings.workflow.workspaceDefaults.titl.note: A setting's title (Settings → Version Control): the workflow options the open workspace's projects start from, over Hive defaults (HI-1768). The window shows the workspace's name beside it.

settings.workspace.antivirus.desc.text: Whether Microsoft Defender scans the workspace's folders as Hive's work changes them (builds, tests, git, worktrees), and the exclusions Hive can add for them, with your consent.
settings.workspace.antivirus.desc.note: What the setting "Antivirus scanning" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.antivirus.tip.text: Hive checks without administrator rights, so Defender may not show its exclusions (unknown). Adding or removing exclusions asks for administrator rights once. Hive only ever offers these folders: the workspace, its worktrees folder once it exists, and its test area for people developing Hive. It never changes other antivirus products.
settings.workspace.antivirus.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Antivirus scanning" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.commands.desc.text: This workspace's own commands: run one by hand (here, or Run Command in the command palette), or pick it, or one of Hive's, for when this workspace opens or closes.
settings.workspace.commands.desc.note: What the setting "Commands" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace, HI-1954).

settings.workspace.commands.tip.text: Saved in the workspace's .hive/workspace.json, which Hive keeps out of version control. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.commands.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Commands" (Settings → Workspace, HI-1954). Keep the file path as it is.

settings.workspace.commands.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Workspace): the user's own named commands for this workspace (HI-1954).

settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc.text: Restore one to bring it back with its cards (and, for a removed one, the handovers packed into its folder). A folder that has left the workspace can be forgotten.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc.note: What the setting "Hidden and removed projects" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip.text: Project → Remove Project… hides a project, removes it from Hive (its folder keeps its handovers and cards in .hive/removed, so it can move to another workspace) or deletes it (to the Recycle Bin). Deleted projects are not listed here: restore the folder from the Recycle Bin and Hive sees it as a new project.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Hidden and removed projects" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.onClose.desc.text: The commands Hive runs, in order, as this workspace closes: its window closes, another workspace opens in it, or Hive quits. Hive waits for them, showing them running.
settings.workspace.onClose.desc.note: What the setting "When this workspace closes, run" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace; HI-1954: a list of the user's commands).

settings.workspace.onClose.tip.text: Pick them from Commands above. '{workspace}' becomes the workspace's folder, '{name}' its name and '{reason}' why it closes: window, switch, quit, or update when Hive restarts to install an update (only with that box ticked). Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.onClose.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "When this workspace closes, run" (Settings → Workspace; HI-1954). '{workspace}', '{name}' and '{reason}' are placeholders the user writes in a command, and window, switch, quit and update are the values {reason} becomes: keep them all as they are (the quotes around each placeholder keep it from being read as one of this text). Commands is the title of the setting above.

settings.workspace.onClose.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Workspace): a command of the user's that Hive runs as the open workspace closes.

settings.workspace.onOpen.desc.text: The commands Hive runs, in order, as this workspace opens: a local server or a database its agents need, say. Its agents start once they're done, or once you choose Don't wait.
settings.workspace.onOpen.desc.note: What the setting "When this workspace opens, run" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace, HI-1954). Don't wait is the name of a button of the dialog Hive shows.

settings.workspace.onOpen.tip.text: Pick them from Commands above. '{reason}' becomes open. If one fails, Hive asks: Rerun, Skip it and continue, or Stop here; a command ticked "The commands after this need it" leads with Stop here. Only you can set them: the Assistant can't change them.
settings.workspace.onOpen.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "When this workspace opens, run" (Settings → Workspace, HI-1954). '{reason}' is a placeholder the user writes in a command, and open the value it becomes: keep both as they are. Rerun, Skip it and continue and Stop here are buttons of the dialog; the quoted text is a checkbox's label: use their translations.

settings.workspace.onOpen.title.note: A setting's title (Settings → Workspace): the user's commands Hive runs as the workspace opens (HI-1954).

settings.workspace.storage.desc.text: What Hive keeps for each of the workspace's projects (the biggest first) and the Hive Assistant: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and worktrees. Storage opens a project's page, with Clean Up… and Purge…; Purge… here removes everything Hive keeps for the sessions of the whole workspace.
settings.workspace.storage.desc.note: What the setting "Storage" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace). Clean Up… and Purge… are buttons: use their names as translated there.

settings.workspace.storage.tip.text: Measured in the background, a project at a time. The coding agents' own transcripts (in ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot) aren't counted. Hidden projects aren't included.
settings.workspace.storage.tip.note: The info tip of the setting "Storage" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.
